BactoCloud is the secure cloud platform for BactoSense users, enabling real-time visibility, remote access, and intelligent data integration across all water monitoring operations.

BactoSense initiates an outbound internet connection to BactoCloud. The connection can use BactoLink, a 4G/5G access point or wired internet. Multiple instruments can share an internet connection behind NAT; no VPN or inbound port forwarding is required. Requirement Configuration Network addressing Provide a working IP address, subnet mask, gateway and DNS resolver. DHCP and static addressing are supported. Confirm static settings with the network administrator. Outbound access Allow outbound access to *.bactocloud.com and *.bnovate.net from the instrument network. Bandwidth Plan for more than 1 Mbit/s. Data usage Allow roughly 0.5–1 GB per month per instrument measuring hourly. Historical synchronization, diagnostics and software updates add traffic. Time synchronization Configure an approved time source where required so event timestamps can be correlated. Browser proxy A proxy used by BactoCloud users must support secure WebSocket connections to BactoCloud. Keep the instrument's local web interface on a controlled plant network and do not expose instrument services to the public internet. Existing PLC, Modbus and I/O connections can remain in use. For instrument configuration, see Network configuration and Set NTP Servers.

Visit www.bactocloud.com/register, enter the requested account details and complete email verification. Registration creates your personal account; organization membership connects it to an instrument fleet. If you received an invitation, follow its link and sign in or register with the exact email address that was invited. After accepting the invitation, select the organization from the header. To create an organization for your own fleet, open the organization selector in the header and choose New Organisation. Enter its name, choose its time zone and applications, then select Create Organisation. Select the intended organization before generating an enrolment code.

Enrolment connects an instrument to one BactoCloud organization. You need permission to enrol instruments in that organization and an admin account on the instrument. Use the instrument's touchscreen or an approved VNC remote view of that touchscreen. An instrument can belong to only one organization at a time. Before enrolment, check the installed BactoSense software: Rev3 instruments require 3.1.0 or later, and Rev2 instruments require 2.4.0 or later. Individual cloud features can require newer software or instrument options. If you cannot install an update locally, contact your service channel before proceeding.

Sign in to BactoCloud and use the organization selector to choose the organization that should own the instrument. Open the organization selector in the header, choose Organisation Settings, then Instruments in the sidebar. Select Enrol instrument. This action is also available on the empty fleet page when no instruments are enrolled. Review the enrolment explanation and software requirement, then select Generate new code. Write down or copy the generated code. The Enrolment codes section lists existing codes and their expiry dates. Use a code before its listed expiry date, or generate a replacement if it has expired. Each code belongs to the organization in which it was generated. If the enrolment action is unavailable, ask an organization administrator to check your access.

On the BactoSense Home screen, select Settings in the bottom toolbar. Select System settings in the Settings menu. Select BactoCloud to open Cloud Settings. Select Enroll, enter the code generated in BactoCloud and confirm the entry. Follow the on-screen messages, then check that Enrolled shows Yes and Organisation names the intended organization. If BactoCloud is unavailable, check your local user role and whether Demo mode or PLC mode is active.

documents.t: In BactoCloud, use the header's organization selector to open Organisation Settings → Instruments and check the instrument's name, serial number and reported connection state. Confirm that its latest status and measurements arrive. Last seen at is the time of the latest status received by BactoCloud; it does not test the current network connection. If the instrument is missing, verify that you generated the code under the intended organization and completed the instrument procedure. If a code is rejected or the instrument already belongs to another organization, ask an organization administrator or support for help. If status or measurements stop arriving, note the instrument serial number, software version, timestamp and last successful upload. Ask the network administrator to verify DNS and outbound connectivity from the instrument network using the IT requirements. The organization's instrument inventory also shows Enrolled since. Users with instrument deletion permission can select the row action Unlink Instrument from organisation. Before unlinking, export any measurements you need to retain. The confirmation warns that unlinking stops uploads and deletes the existing cloud measurements. Verify the target instrument, enter its serial number in the confirmation and select Unlink instrument.

An up-to-date list of all bNovate representatives is available online at www.bnovate.com/distribution-partners. Description of what you did when trying to solve the problem yourself. Documentation of the third-party products you use in conjunction with the BactoSense. Description of operation conditions (place, power supply, measured medium, temperature etc.). This user manual. Export of the last measurements when the error occurred, see Exporting measurements.

The “Special import/export” function allows users to export either all measurement data from the instrument, or to export only diagnostics data which can be interpreted by service technicians. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. Press the Special export import button. 3. Connect a USB mass storage device. The USB flash drive should be formatted in FAT32. If needed, press the Refresh USB list button until the device is displayed. 4. The name of the folder which will be created on the USB device is displayed in the Folder name field. Enter a new folder name if desired. 5. • To export all data, press the Export all button. • To export diagnostics data, press the Export diagnostics button. • To export settings, press the Export diagnostics button. Do not remove the USB mass storage device during the data transfer. Exporting all data can take several hours. If the available storage capacity of the USB mass storage device is too small, a notification will be shown. 6. After completion of the export, press the OK button and remove the USB device.

documents.t: BactoSense data can be remotely accessed using the FTP protocol (RFC 3659). FTP authentication uses the username/password pairs used in the GUI of the instrument. Default account names are: basic, advanced, and admin. The CSV and Excel files are generated on-the-fly, and thus always contain the latest measurement data. Figure 12-1 The Manage services view of the BactoSense user interface. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. • Install an FTP client on the device you want to use to retrieve data, e.g. your laptop. • Alternatively, the Windows file explorer can be used. 2. Connect the BactoSense via Ethernet to a safe network (e.g. LAN). Connect your device to the same network. For information about network configurations (i.e. static and dynamic IP settings), refer to Network configuration. 3. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 4. Press the System settings button. 5. Press the System services button. 6. Make sure the Enable FTP data access check box is checked. 7. Choose a port for the FTP server. The default port is port 21. 8. Press Apply to save the changes. If a reboot is requested, press Reboot now. Only needed in case you changed the configuration. 9. On the Home screen, press Settings, then System info to retrieve the IP address of the BactoSense. For information about network configurations (i.e. static and dynamic IP settings), refer to Network configuration. 10. For FTP client: Open the client and enter the login details. For the Windows file explorer: Enter the following address in the address bar: ftp://user:password@ip:port • User/username: Username to log in to the BactoSense • Password: Password to log in to the BactoSense • Host/ip: IP address of the BactoSense • Port: Port configured in System services view (see figure 12-1)

The HTTP and HTTPS servers are enabled by default and available through a web browser or any HTTP request library. Use the following procedure to retrieve specific files via HTTP or HTTPS. As an alternative, consider the web interface (Web User Interface) or FTP (Retrieve data via FTP). WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Connect the BactoSense via Ethernet to a safe network (e.g. LAN). Connect your device to the same network. For information about network configurations (i.e. static and dynamic IP settings), refer to Network configuration. 2. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 3. Press the System settings button. 4. Press the System services button. 5. For HTTP: Make sure the Enable HTTP web access check box is checked. For HTTPS: Make sure the Enable HTTPS web access check box is checked. 6. Choose a port for the HTTP or HTTPS server. The default port for HTTP is 80. The default port for HTTPS is 443. 7. Press Apply to save the changes. If a reboot is requested, press Reboot now. Only needed in case you changed the configuration. 8. On the Home screen, press Settings, then System info to retrieve the IP address of the BactoSense. 9. Open a web browser on your device and enter the target file address into the address field. The file address has the following form: For HTTP: http://ipaddress:port/export/filename.extension?hash=myhash Example: http://192.168.1.2/export/history_auto.xlsx?hash=QWRtaW46MTExMQ For HTTPS: https://ipaddress:port/export/filename.extension?hash=myhash Example: https://192.168.1.2/export/history_auto.xlsx?hash=QWRtaW46MTExMQ Name Description ipaddress Local IP address of the instrument port Port of the HTTP or HTTPS server (by default 80 and 443, respectively) filename Name of the target file. Example: history_auto extension File extension (csv, xlsx,pdf) myhash Security key containing user identification. The key is unique to any user-password combination. It is possible to find the key in the web interface (Web User Interface) by copying the link shown when downloading a file. For example: hash=QWRtaW46MTExMQ

documents.t: Virtual Network Computing (VNC) is a graphical desktop-sharing system to remotely control another computer. It transmits the keyboard and mouse input from one computer to another, relaying the graphical-screen updates, over a network. The embedded VNC server in the BactoSense is capable of sharing the user interface over the local area network (LAN) only (exception: remote access using a VPN). Restrict VNC access VNC is an insecure protocol and is not recommended outside of a local network or with a VPN connection. Close VNC after use A VNC connection can slow down the user interface since it is very taxing in terms of processing power. Be sure to close your VNC connection after use. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Install a VNC client on your computer. 2. Connect the BactoSense via Ethernet to a safe network (LAN). Connect your computer to the same network. For information about network configurations (i.e. static and dynamic IP settings), refer to Network configuration. 3. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 4. Press the System settings button. 5. Press the System services button. 6. Make sure the Enable VNC remote control check box is checked. 7. Choose a port for the VNC server. The default port is port 5900. 8. Press Apply to save the changes. If a reboot is requested, press Reboot now. Only needed in case you changed the configuration. 9. On the Home screen, press Settings, then System info to retrieve the IP address of the BactoSense. 10. Open the VNC client on your computer and connect to the BactoSense using the IP address and port identified previously. Your VNC client may allow you to change connection settings to optimize the speed of the connection if needed. 11. After finishing, return to System services, disable the VNC checkbox and press Apply. If a reboot is requested, press Reboot now. The VNC connection can slow down the user interface on the BactoSense.

The BactoSense can be operated via the Modbus Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). The following requirements must be met: The computer and/or the management or control system must be compatible with Modbus TCP. The computer and/or the management or control system must have software that can properly process the data provided by the BactoSense. The BactoSense must have the Modbus TCP service activated under Home → Settings → System settings → System services. The BactoSense must be connected to the bus system. To be able to work with the Modbus TCP, the network settings must be set correctly. Additional information The Modbus TCP interface is integrated by default in the BactoSense. The Ethernet socket is located at the right-hand side of the instrument. The address table necessary for programming can be found in the Modbus TCP address list. All registers are encoded big-endian. Modbus TCP communication runs on port 502. The error code lists can be found in Non-critical errors and Critical errors. Modbus TCP can be used for time synchronisation. Follow the instructions in Set NTP Servers and select Modbus TCP as a sync source.

The power button of the BactoSense is located on the right hand-side of the instrument. Figure 8-1 Power button of the BactoSense Check the power supply Before switching the BactoSense on, make sure that the instrument is connected to a stable power supply meeting the requirements described in Connecting the BactoSense to power. Switching on To switch the BactoSense on, shortly press on the power button. The power button LED lights up constantly and after a few seconds, the welcome screen is displayed on the user interface. Switching off If you are logged in and want to switch the BactoSense off, tap on the logout button on the top right corner of the user interface and select Power off. If you want to switch off from the login page itself, press the power button for 10 seconds. Disconnect power safely To disconnect the BactoSense from power, first switch the instrument off. Then unplug the power supply unit from the mains power source, before unplugging the power supply plug from the BactoSense.

BactoSense operation requires users to log in. Different user roles with different permissions are available. The user role permissions are listed in User roles and permissions. All logins are password protected. Login and logout can be performed using the login button displayed in the top right corner of the user interface. The currently active user role is displayed next to that button.

WORK STEP 1. Press the login button on the top right corner of the user interface, or the login bar at the bottom in case you switched on the instrument. 2. For BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID in the standard configuration: Select one of the user profiles Basic, Advanced or Admin. For BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID upgraded with the Management package (see Management package) and advanced user management mode activated (see Activating advanced user management mode), enter your user ID. 3. Enter the password and press OK. If you don’t know the password, ask your Admin user. In a new instrument no passwords are set. In that case, follow the procedure described in Setting and changing passwords. 4. After logging in, you see the BactoSense user interface. 5. To log out, follow the procedure described in Manual logout.

WORK STEP 1. Make sure all processes (e.g. measurements or cleanings) have completed. The idle state of the instrument is indicated on the left hand-side of the top bar of the BactoSense user interface. 2. Press the logout button in the top right corner of the user interface. 3. Select Log out / Lock screen. 4. To log in again, follow the procedure described in Login.

It is possible to configure an automated logout after predefined period of inactivity. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the Users button. 4. Press the Settings button. 5. Configure the desired auto-logout time period. 6. Press Save.

With the Advanced User Management feature, an instrument admin can create different users and assign different user roles (Basic, Advanced, Admin). This allows to give different permissions to individual users, and log their activity for the audit trail. Advanced user management mode is available for BactoSense SMART and PURE, and BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID upgraded with the management package (see Management package). WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the System configuration button. 4. Check the Advanced user management mode checkbox. 5. Press Save.

Each user role is password protected. Setting a password at first login Upon initial login with any user role, click OK when being prompted for a password. This action will initiate the guided process for configuring your password. The only exception is the service password, where a preset password is provided. Setting and changing a passwords Each user profile can change its own password. Admin users are allowed to change passwords from other user profiles. The following procedure describes how to change passwords. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings. Basic users press Change password; Advanced and Admin users press System settings, then Users. 2. Select the user profile you want to edit, then press Edit. Basic and Advanced users can change their own PIN. Admin users can also change the PIN of Basic and Advanced users. 3. Press Change PIN. Enter the new PIN in PIN and Confirm PIN, then press Save.

Several password features such as expiration, length etc can be configured. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the Users button. 4. Press the Settings button. 5. Configure the password requirements based on your preferences. 6. Press Save.

The language can only be changed by admin users. WORK STEP 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. Press the Language button. 3. Choose the language and press the OK button. 4. When prompted to reload the user interface, press Reload interface.

Date and time can only be changed by admin users. Automatic time synchronization If time synchronization is enabled, either with NTP servers or through Modbus TCP, your manual date and time settings will be overridden during the next synchronization. Settings can be found under Home > Settings > System settings > Date & time > Time synchronization settings. For setting up NTP server, please refer to Set NTP Servers. WORK STEP 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the Date & time button. 4. Enter the date and time. 5. Select the time zone. 6. Press the Set button.

The device name can only be changed by admin users. WORK STEP 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the System configuration button. 4. Tap the Device name field. 5. Enter the device name using the keyboard and press OK. 6. Press the Save button.

The BactoSense has a built-in auto-restart functionality to automatically recover from temporary power interruptions. Depending on the configuration, the instrument can simply restart, but also return to operation by performing a self-cleaning process and restarting an Online mode series. WORK STEP 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the System configuration button. 4. Select your automatic power-on preferences. Note: Self-cleaning only occurs if the power has been interrupted during a measurement. 5. Press the Save button.

You can turn on audible notifications to indicate the end of a manual measurement or maintenance process, alarm or error. The notification is one or several beeping sounds from the instrument. WORK STEP 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the System configuration button. 4. Activate Sound notifications. 5. Press the Save button.

Settings are exported to a USB drive as per Export settings, diagnostics, or all to USB device. The settings are compiled to a timestamped file ending with *.bnv. In order to import the settings in a new instrument, or as a backup, it is necessary to copy the *.bnv file at the root of the USB drive, or in the directory the file was exported to. If multiple copies of the settings are located in one USB drive, the system will use the most recent one. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. 3. Press the Special export import button. 4. Connect a USB drive. If needed, press the Refresh USB list button until the drive is detected. Make sure the *.bnv file is at the root of the USB drive. The USB drive should be formatted in FAT32, which is the common standard. 5. Press the Import settings button. 6. Select the settings you want to import. Measurement settings include gate sets, IO settings, alarms, and date and time settings. Network settings include IP, DNS, and NTP addresses 7. Press Import settings, then Reboot now in the confirmation message, and wait until the device reboots.

The following rules apply to alarms: Only Advanced and Admin users can change the alarm settings. Alarms are only active in the Online mode. BactoSense records alarms in the following ways: A popup is displayed in the graphical user interface An alarm bell icon appears in the top bar if the last measurement exceeded the alarm threshold. The alarm is shown in the measurement summary when viewing a result. A signal can be sent out to a PLC through digital outputs (configurable). Figure 8-2 Alarm configuration in the BactoSense graphical user interface. 1 Select, enable or disable alarms. Users can configure up to 9 alarms. 2 Name of the currently selected alarm. 3 Source of the alarm: Which measurement result should be evaluated. See figure 8-3. 4 Condition: Trigger the alarm when the measured parameter is larger than (>) or smaller than (<) the threshold. 5 Threshold 6 Display: If checked, a line will be shown on the Online mode plot, in the selected color. Figure 8-3 BactoSense alarm sources. For a selected source, a condition and a threshold are set. In the example above, an alarm is triggered on a certain cartridge filling level. The following procedure describes how to configure the alarm: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Online mode settings button. 3. Press the Alarm button. 4. Activate, select and configure the alarms (according to figure 8-2 and figure 8-3). By default, no alarms are active. 5. Press Save to save the alarm configuration.

Network settings Ask your network administrator for the correct settings. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the Network button. 4. A: For Dynamic IP check the DHCP check box (1). Note: This is the preferred configuration for most cases when the BactoSense is connected to a router or switch. B: For Static IP uncheck the DHCP check box (1) and enter the desired network configuration (2). Note: This is the preferred configuration when the BactoSense is directly connected to a laptop via Ethernet. Make sure to also adjust the network configuration on the laptop accordingly. 5. Press the Save button. 6. Press the Reboot now button.

Network Time Protocol (NTP) is a computer network protocol which is used to synchronise time on computers across a network. By default, these are set to synchronise to the Network Time Foundation servers (ntp.org). You have the possibility to set custom NTP servers in the Date & time menu. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the Date & time button. 4. Press the Time synchronization settings button. 5. Select the desired Sync Source. Additional information Time synchronisation can be done via NTP server or Modbus TCP. More information about Modbus TCP can be found in Modbus TCP 6. Update NTP servers. 7 Press the OK button. Additional information Press Test NTP to check whether the configured servers are reachable. Press OK to save the synchronization settings.

Figure 8-4 The Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. The Home screen shows the latest measurement result. Press Settings to open the settings menu. The BactoSense user interface is divided into 3 main sections: A Top bar B Content view C Action bar The main elements of the user interface are: 1 Home or return button. To navigate through the menu. 2 Operation mode (Manual or Online) Instrument status (currently active process) 3 Current view 4 Top bar status icons, see Top bar status icons. 5 User Role Current time 6 Logout or power off 7 Results: display the measurement results for the selected mode. 8 Mode: choose Online mode for continuous measurements using the online sampling device, or Manual mode for measuring grab samples using the manual sampling device. 9 Measure: open the measurement wizard and choose an analysis protocol (Manual mode). Depending on the user role, some options may not be visible or disabled.

The BactoSense cartridges contain the reagents required for measuring and maintaining the instrument clean. Available cartridge types are TCC (Total Cell Count), ICC (Intact Cell Count), EBC (E. coli Cell Count), ACC (Active Cell Count), CBC (Coliform Cell Count), and NBC (Enterococcus Cell Count). The following sections explain cartridge handling. Cartridge storage, transportation and refill are described in Storage, Transport and Disposal.

When handling the cartridge, the following instructions must be followed: Table 8-3 Cartridge handling instructions Follow the procedures described in this manual. Store and ship between 15 °C – 25 °C (59 °F – 77 °F). The optimal temperature is 15 °C (59 °F). Wear nitrile gloves when handling the cartridge. Store and ship between 20 % and 60 % relative humidity. Wear safety glasses when handling the cartridge. The cartridge is intended for refill. Ship, install and store in the indicated orientation Do not throw the cartridge into the trash.

The cartridge filling levels and expiration date can be retrieved from several sources. The cartridge icon shown in the top bar of the user interface constantly indicates the approximate cartridge filling level. In case the cartridge is about to expire, the cartridge icon displays this too. Explanations of the different icons can be found in Top bar status icons. If you need more information, press Settings on the Home screen, then press System info. Under Cartridge capacity remaining you see how full the cartridge still is (in percent), and under Cartridge expiration date you see when the cartridge expires. The same information can also be retrieved from the web interface (see Web User Interface)
documents.s: 8.9.2 Checking the filling level and expiration date of a cartridge

documents.t: The BactoSense cartridge is installed in a dedicated cartridge compartment of the instrument. A door closes the cartridge compartment. The cartridge door must only be opened for removing and installing cartridges. Figure 8-5 The BactoSense cartridge compartment can be opened by removing two 7 mm hex nuts using the supplied hex nut driver. 1 7 mm hex nuts to secure cartridge compartment door 2 Cartridge compartment door Use the correct door tool Open and close the cartridge compartment door only with the dedicated 7 mm hex nut driver. After opening the cartridge compartment door, the user has access to the cartridge and the connectors which connect the cartridge to the BactoSense. Figure 8-6 Overview of an installed cartridge. The mobility of the cartridge is secured with a fixation latch on top (4), and the cartridge is connected to the instrument with multiple fluidic (5 - 8) and one electronic connector (9). When no cartridge is inserted, the fluidic and electronic connectors can be secured using the removable connector rack (10). 1 BactoSense instrument 2 Cartridge 3 Cartridge handle 4 Cartridge fixation latch 5 Dye connector (green) 6 Bleach connector (red) 7 Waste connector (black or beige) 8 Rinse connector (blue) 9 Electronic connector 10 Removable connector rack 11 Cartridge compartment door Protect the unused connector The BactoSense has five fluidic connectors. Depending on the cartridge type, only four or all five fluidic connectors are needed. In case of TCC or ICC cartridges, make sure the unused fifth connector is always mounted to the connector rack to prevent contamination.

The following procedure describes the exchange of cartridges. Use this procedure if you want to remove and directly install another cartridge. If you only want to remove a cartridge and not install another one, follow the instruction in Removing a cartridge. The duration of the cartridge exchange is approximately 35 min. Follow the cartridge wizard Strictly follow the procedure in the on-screen wizard. Do not remove or install cartridges without this procedure. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Have the replacement cartridge ready and adjusted to ambient temperature. 2. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 3. Press the Maintenance button. Basic users skip this step. 4. Press the Cartridge change button. 5. Select Change cartridge. 6. Follow the cartridge wizard Confirm to follow the instructions of the on- screen wizard. Only open the cartridge compartment door when instructed. Adhere to the general cartridge handling instruction in General instructions for cartridge handling. Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Tightly seal the fluidic connectors of the old cartridge with the attached plugs before removing it. Make sure the cartridge compartment door is tightly closed and secured at the end. Skipping the cartridge wizard Only very experienced users mastering safe cartridge operations are allowed to skip the on-screen instructions. In case of TCC or ICC cartridges, make sure the unused fifth connector is always mounted to the connector rack to prevent contamination. 7. Handling the removed cartridge • If you wish to store the removed cartridge, refer to the storage instructions in Storage of the cartridge. • If you wish to refill the removed cartridge, refer to the refill instructions in Returning a cartridge for refill.

This procedure is intended for the removal of a cartridge, without immediate installation of another cartridge. If you want to exchange cartridges, follow the procedure described in Change cartridges. The duration of the cartridge removal is approximately 5 min. Follow the cartridge wizard Strictly follow the procedure in the on-screen wizard. Do not remove or install cartridges without this procedure. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. Basic users skip this step. 3. Press the Cartridge change button. 4. Select Remove cartridge. 5. Follow the cartridge wizard Confirm to follow the instructions of the on- screen wizard. Only open the cartridge compartment door when instructed. Adhere to the general cartridge handling instruction in General instructions for cartridge handling. Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Tightly seal the fluidic connectors of the old cartridge with the attached plugs before removing it. Make sure the cartridge compartment door is tightly closed and secured at the end. Skipping the cartridge wizard Only very experienced users mastering safe cartridge operations are allowed to skip the on-screen instructions. 6. Handling of the removed cartridge • If you wish to store the removed cartridge, refer to the storage instructions in Storage of the cartridge. • If you wish to refill the removed cartridge, refer to the refill instructions in Returning a cartridge for refill. The top bar of the user interface indicates that no cartridge is connected. In the Settings menu, Maintenance is highlighted; Basic users see the highlighted Cartridge change button directly.

This procedure is intended for the installation of a cartridge, when no other cartridge is installed in the BactoSense. If there is already a cartridge and you want to exchange cartridges, follow the procedure described in Change cartridges. The duration of the cartridge installation is approximately 30 min. Follow the cartridge wizard Strictly follow the procedure of the on-screen wizard. Do not remove or install cartridges without this procedure. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Have the new cartridge ready and adjusted to ambient temperature. 2. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 3. Press the Maintenance button. The Maintenance button is highlighted in orange in case no cartridge is installed. Basic users skip this step. 4. Press the Cartridge change button. 5. Select Install cartridge. 6. Follow the cartridge wizard Confirm to follow the instructions of the on- screen wizard. Only open the cartridge compartment door when instructed. Adhere to the general cartridge handling instruction in General instructions for cartridge handling. Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Make sure the cartridge compartment door is tightly closed and secured at the end. Skipping the cartridge wizard Only very experienced users mastering safe cartridge operations are allowed to skip the on-screen instructions. In case of TCC or ICC cartridges, make sure the unused fifth connector is always mounted to the connector rack to prevent contamination. 7. After following through all steps of the on- screen wizard, the new cartridge is properly initialized. The cartridge status is indicated with a cartridge symbol in the top bar of the user interface, see Top bar status icons.

The BactoSense can be operated with either the manual or the online sampling device. The following procedure describes the exchange of sampling devices. Sampling device storage information can be found in Storage of the sampling devices. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Remove the mounted sampling device according to the instructions in Removal of the online sampling device (online sampling device) or Removal of the manual sampling device (manual sampling device) 2. Install the new sampling device according to the instructions in Installation of the online sampling device (online sampling device) or Installation of the manual sampling device (manual sampling device).

When switching to the manual sampling device, the online sampling device has to be removed. Follow the procedure below to safely remove the device and prepare it for storage. Wear protective gloves Avoid contamination of the equipment. Wear nitrile gloves when handling samples, sampling devices and any components which come in contact with them. WORK STEP 1. Terminate any ongoing measurement series, as described in Terminating automatic online measurements. 2. Stop the water flow through the sampling device tubings and sampling device. 3. Carefully unscrew the knurled sampling device fixation ring until the sampling device can be removed. 4. Remove the online sampling device. Make sure the white sealing plug still sits tightly in the connector of the sampling device. If not, it may have remained in the BactoSense sampling device connector. In this case carefully remove it with tweezers and place it back in the sampling device. 5. Disconnect and drain the inlet and outlet tubings from the water source and the sampling device body. 6. Inspect the inlet and outlet tubings for contamination and damage. Only reuse clean and intact tubings. 7. If you want to store the sampling device, place the device and the tubings separately in a clean and dry plastic bags and follow the storage instructions in Storage of the sampling devices. 8. To mount now the manual sampling device, see Installation of the manual sampling device.
documents.s: 8.10.1 Removal of the online sampling device

documents.t: When switching to the online sampling device, the manual sampling device has to be removed. Follow the procedure below to safely remove the device and prepare it for storage. Wear protective gloves Avoid contamination of the equipment. Wear nitrile gloves when handling samples, sampling devices and any components which come in contact with them. WORK STEP 1. Perform a cleaning of the manual sampling device: If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation, otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning. 2. After finishing, attach a clean and empty 5 mL screw-cap tube or the Washstation to the sampling device. 3. Carefully unscrew the knurled sampling device fixation ring on top of the device until the sampling device can be removed. 4. Remove the manual sampling device. Make sure the white sealing plug still sits tightly in the connector of the sampling device. If not, it may have remained in the BactoSense sampling device connector. In this case, carefully remove it with tweezers and place it back in the sampling device. 5. If you want to store the sampling device, place it in a clean and dry plastic bag and follow the storage instructions in Storage of the sampling devices. 6. To mount now the online sampling device, follow the procedure in Installation of the online sampling device.

documents.t: Qualification is a process to ensure the BactoSense operates as intended. Different options are available. To do a fully automated quick check of the instrument status, perform the self-check procedure described in Automatic self-check. This test does not require any reagents or user interaction, is very quick and checks the integrity and communication between the different modules of the BactoSense. To assess the cleanliness of the BactoSense and rule out a contamination, perform the cleanliness verification procedure in Cleanliness verification. For operational environments requiring system suitability testing, use the System Suitability Test Kit (SST Kit) and follow the procedure in its user manual. For other environments, an instrument qualification using the Validation kit is recommended in the following situations: After shipping the instrument or other long-distance transport, exposing the instrument to vibration or shock. After storing the instrument for more than one month. If there are indications that measurement results could be erroneous.

WORK STEP 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device. 2. Perform a cleaning of the sampling device with two replications: If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation, otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning. 3. Prepare the blank sample in a 5 mL screw-cap tube. There are two options: A) Use cell-free water, e.g. a sterile solution aliquot from the Validation Kit. If you use the sterile solution aliquot from the Validation Kit, remove the cap of the aliquot and place the aliquot in an empty 5 mL screw-cap tube, as described in the user manual of the Validation Kit. B) Take a still mineral water and filter twice using a membrane filter with a pore size of 0.22 µm or smaller. 4. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 5. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 6. Select Prime from the list of available protocols. 7. Press the Next button. 8. Remove the tube or Washstation from the manual sampling device and attach the blank sample. 9. Press the Start button to run the Prime protocol. 10. After completion of the Prime, press the New button to navigate back to the list of protocols. 11. Select Water Analysis from the list of available protocols. 12. Configure two replications. 13. Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field, entering the name and pressing OK. 14. Verify that the ICC or TCC default gate is configured and change it otherwise by pressing into the Gates field. 15. Press the Next button. 16. Press the Start button and wait for the two measurements to complete. 17. After finishing, press the Next button to review the results. 18. Look at the results and compare them to the reference values indicated below. The BactoSense is clean if the following criteria are fulfilled: • For TCC cartridges: TCC [/mL] < 300 • For ICC cartridges: ICC [/mL] < 100 19. If the cell concentrations are higher than the specified limits, apply the following procedure: • Repeat the procedure with a freshly prepared blank sample. • Repeat the procedure after a decontamination using the Cleaning Kit (see Consumables). • If the test keeps failing, contact bNovate support or your local service representative. 20. After finishing, attach a clean and empty 5 mL screw-cap tube or the Washstation to the manual sampling device.

Demo mode can be used when demonstrating the device or when learning how to navigate the menus and use the functions. When it is activated, the instrument reboots into a special mode that displays demonstration data (the owner’s measurement results are hidden). All the instrument’s functions are replaced by simulations that never move the hardware or modify the results database. This means protocols can be started without needing to load a sample, and users can pretend to delete or re-gate results without ever changing the data. If the demo mode is activated, the message Demo is displayed in the upper middle of the screen. When the instrument is reverted to normal mode, the owner’s data is shown again, and all functions are active again. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. Press the Demo mode button. 3. Select the Activate demo mode checkbox. 4. Press the Save and restart button. 5. The device reboots automatically. To return into normal mode, follow the same procedure, but uncheck the Activate demo mode box.

Factory reset reverts most of the instrument settings to the factory values: Gating limits, measurement interval, default protocol names, users, language and network settings. This option is accessible only by the Admin and Service users. The following procedure describes how to perform a factory reset: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button, then the Factory reset button. 3. Use the check boxes to select which parameters you wish to reset: • Instrument settings • Measurements incl. errors and logs • both Additional information Service logs, validation results and the software update his- tory are not deleted. 4. Press Reset the device and reboot, then confirm with Yes.

Intended use The intended use of the BactoSense is to measure the concentration of microorganisms in water. In particular, the instrument has been developed to count and characterise bacterial populations. Term Explanation ACC Active Cell Count. The ACC cartridge measures metabolically active cells using an enzymatic assay. ACC is the total number of active cells inside the ACC gate. CBC Coliform Cell Count. Number of coliform cells counted in the sample. Cartridge Refillable container of reagents needed for BactoSense operation EBC E. coli Cell Count. Number of E. coli cells counted in the sample. FCS Flow Cytometry Standard (FCS) is a data file standard for the reading and writing of data from flow cytometry experiments. The FCS specification has traditionally been developed and maintained by the International Society for Advancement of Cytometry (ISAC). FCS used to be the only widely adopted file format in flow cytometry. FL1 Fluorescence signal 1 (530 nm) FL2 Fluorescence signal 2 (715 nm) FSC Forward scatter, also known as Small Angle Light Scattering. A detector measures the light scattered from microorganisms and other particles at small angles. Gate Gates are tools for data analysis of a subset of data points in flow cytometry. HNA High Nucleic Acid. Bacteria with a large amount of DNA which produce a strong fluorescence emission. HNAC High Nucleic Acid Count. The number of HNA bacteria inside the TCC or ICC gate, and above the HNA / LNA limit. HNAP [%] High Nucleic Acid Percentage. The percentage of HNA bacteria relative to the cell count. ICC Intact Cell Count. Total number of intact bacteria inside of the ICC gate. LNA Low Nucleic Acid. Bacteria with a lower amount of DNA which produce a weaker fluorescence emission than HNA bacteria. LNAC Low Nucleic Acid Count. The number of LNA bacteria inside the TCC or ICC gate below the HNA / LNA limit. Manual Sampling Device Connection module, allowing manual sampling with the BactoSense Online. NBC Enterococcus Cell Count. Number of Enterococcus cells counted in the sample. Online Sampling Device Connection module to a water line, allowing online sampling with the BactoSense Online. SSC Side scatter, also known as Large Angle Light Scattering. A detector measures the light scattered from microorganisms and other particles at 90 degrees. TCC Total Cell Count. Total number of bacteria detected inside the TCC gate.

Before installation Attention Before working on the instrument, carefully read the safety points. It is forbidden to modify or repair the BactoSense. Perform the work steps in the exact order instructed. When replacing parts, use only genuine original parts supplied or recommended by bNovate.

Carefully follow the procedure below to unpack the BactoSense instrument from its packaging. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Open the box and remove the lid. 2. Remove the compartments with accessories. 3. Carefully remove the BactoSense from the box. 4. Keep the packaging and foams for future use.

The BactoSense can be operated as a bench top instrument on a flat surface, or mounted to a wall or panel. Choose a suitable location Note the following points for selecting an appropriate operating location: The BactoSense shall be installed in a vibration-free environment. The power supply must be stable, without spikes or interruptions. The BactoSense should not be exposed to direct sunlight during operation. In case of electromagnetic interference from a nearby object affecting the touchscreen (not responsive or flickering), relocate the BactoSense.

The following procedure describes the mounting of the BactoSense to a vertical wall or panel: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Install two M8 screws at the same height, separated horizontally by 265 mm (10.4”) on a wall. The screw head diameter needs to be between 12 mm and 18 mm (0.47” – 0.71”) Secure wall mounting The fixation must carry at least 60 kg (132 lbs). 2. Adjust the distance of the screws head and the wall according to the picture on the right. X: Wall Y: Screw 3. Mount the BactoSense on the wall using its wall mounting system (red arrows). Tighten the two screws such that the BactoSense is firmly attached to the wall.

documents.t: Use the original power supply The BactoSense must be operated using the supplied original power supply unit to ensure: Compliance with the applicable standards for safety, EMC, ingress protection and RoHS, as listed in Compliance and applied standards. Instrument performance according to bNovate instrument validation protocols. Warranty coverage. Operation with alternative power supply units requires specific evaluation and permission by bNovate. Stable power supply An uninterrupted and stable power supply as specified in Technical data must be guaranteed. The power supply comes in an IP67 enclosure and a cable with either a plug type J, type E or type G. For connecting the BactoSense to power using one of these plugs supplied by bNovate, follow the instructions in Connecting using the standard plug of the power supply unit. For the connection using a different plug or power connectors, use the procedure described in Modifying the standard power supply unit with a different connector. Keep the power disconnect accessible The electrical plug or an additional circuit breaker should always be accessible to disconnect the main supply. The circuit breaker should respect the standards IEC60947-1 and IEC60947-3 and should protect a current of 10 A to 16 A.

The following procedure describes how to connect the BactoSense to power using the standard power supply unit and power plug of type J, E, G or B. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the power supply unit is dry and does not show any signs of damage. 2. Plug the J, E, G or B-type plug of the power supply unit to a power source supplying the indicated voltage. 3. Remove the cover of the power connector socket on the BactoSense. 4. Insert the power connector plug into the power connector socket. 5. Fasten the power connector plug lock ring (X). If the power connector is connected correctly and the instrument is powered, the instrument power button starts blinking. Disconnect power safely To disconnect the BactoSense from power, first switch the instrument off. Then unplug the power supply unit from the mains power source, before unplugging the power supply plug from the BactoSense.
documents.s: 5.3.1 Connecting using the standard plug of the power supply unit

documents.t: Using a different power connector The following procedure only applies, if the BactoSense shall be connected to a power source with a different plug than what has been delivered together with the standard power supply unit (J, E, G or B). In that case, the power supply unit is opened and the new connector installed manually. Qualified electricians only Only professional electricians are authorized to modify the power supply unit. It is forbidden to modify or repair the BactoSense instrument. Perform the work steps in the exact order instructed. Always use a plug with Protective Earth (PE). Power cable requirements If the power supply cable is longer than 2 m, label it near the plug with the name of the device. If the power supply cable is longer than 20 m, the impedance of PE needs to be smaller than 0.2 Ω. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Disconnect the power supply Ensure that the power supply is not connected to power. Remove the cover of the enclosure by unscrewing the four screws (circles). 2. Remove the C13 connector (A) and unscrew it to open. 3. Open the cable connector (Y) and insert the new cable. Cable lengths and wire cross sections: • 0 – 9 m (0 – 30 ft), 1 mm2 • 9 – 21 m (30 – 69 ft), 1.5 mm2 (maximal) The cable connector is dimensioned for a cable diameter of 3 – 10 mm (0.12” – 0.39”). . 4. Connect protective earth Tighten the 3 wires (N, PE, L) in the electrical terminal and block the cable isolation. Ensure, that a plug with Protective Earth (PE) is used and the device is correctly connected to it. 5. Close the C13 connector (A) using the screw and plug it in the power supply. Tighten the cable connector. Try to pull the cable to assess whether the cable connector is tight enough. 6. Optional: the power supply can be mounted on a wall. M4 screws should be used with a minimum length of 20 mm. With the cover still removed, place the 4 screws and fix the enclosure to the wall. 7. Put the cover of the enclosure back and tighten the four screws to seal it. 8. Connect the power supply unit to power and the instrument as described in Connecting using the standard plug of the power supply unit.

documents.t: The manual sampling device is intended for measuring individual grab samples, collected in 5 mL screw-cap tubes. The following procedure describes how to install the manual sampling device. Figure 5-1 Manual sampling device 1: Positioning pins, 2: Plug, 3: Fixation ring, 4: 5 mL screw-cap tube. Wear protective gloves Avoid contamination of the equipment. Wear nitrile gloves when handling samples, sampling devices and any components which come in contact with them. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Inspect the manual sampling device • Make sure it is free of dust and fibers. If not, clean it with a lint-free tissue wetted with sterile water or ethanol • Make sure the white sealing plug is sitting tightly in the connector 2. Attach an empty 5 mL screw-cap tube or the Washstation at the sampling device. 3. Carefully insert the connector of the sampling device into the sampling device port on the left hand-side of the BactoSense by inserting the metallic positioning pins located inside of the sampling device connector into the openings on the BactoSense sampling device port. 4. Tighten by hand only Then tighten the knurled fixation ring until the sampling device is installed tightly. Finger-tightening only. Do not use any tools. 5. It is recommended to clean the sampling device after installation. If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation, otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning. 6. After the cleaning, it is recommended to perform a Prime prior to measuring the first sample. Follow the procedure in Performing a Prime.
documents.s: 5.4 Installation of the manual sampling device

documents.t: The online sampling device is intended to measure samples continuously at predefined measurement intervals, and it is therefore directly connected to a water source and drain using an inlet and outlet tubing. The following procedure describes how to install the online sampling device. Figure 5-2 Online sampling device 1: Outlet tubing connected to a drain, 2: Inlet tubing connected to a water source, 3: Connector nut, 4: Fixation ring, 5: Positioning pins, 6: Plug. Wear protective gloves Avoid contamination of the equipment. Wear nitrile gloves when handling samples, sampling devices and any components which come in contact with them. Secure tubing connections Firmly attach tubings and sampling device If the plumbing, tubings or sampling device are not tightly assembled or mounted, liquid can flood surrounding areas and cause material damage to nearby objects or infrastructure. All tube junctions must be carefully secured and tightened. The connections should be checked periodically after installation. Connect the outlet to a drain Connect outlet tubing to a drain In drinking water installations, connect the outlet tubing to a drain to make sure that water which has been diverted from the drinking water pipe system is not returned after flowing through the additional fittings, tubings and BactoSense sampling device.
documents.s: 5.5 Installation of the online sampling device

documents.t: The following instructions describe how to attach the inlet and outlet tubings to the body of the online sampling device. Specifications of the tubings can be found in Technical data. The exchange of tubings in case they are contaminated or damaged is described in Replacing online sampling device tubings. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the sampling device is not installed at the BactoSense. 2. Unscrew the nuts of the two connectors on the sampling device. If necessary use a spanner. Be careful not to lose the ferrules located inside the nut. 3. Inspect the two tubings for contamination and damage. Only use clean and intact tubings with straight cuts. 4. For both tubings, insert one end through a nut and a ferrule as illustrated. 5. Attach the blue tubing (outlet) to the connector closer to the attachment port of the sampling device. Attach the transparent tubing (inlet) to the more distant connector to the attachment port of the sampling device. Use a clamp to fasten the nuts. 6. If you want to attach the sampling device, proceed with Installing the online sampling device at the BactoSense.
documents.s: 5.5.1 Attaching the tubings to the online sampling device

documents.t: In this section, the installation of the online sampling device with attached inlet and outlet tubings is described. Figure 5-3 Typical installation for the online analysis mode using the online sampling device. Flow and pressure adjustment​ On-off valve Pressure valve with gauge Flow valve Reduction fittings In and outlet tubings​ Backpressure loop Tubing fixation Horizontal inlet tubing Outlet tubing connected to drain Online sampling device​ Outlet tubing Inlet tubing Inlet conditions: Continuous flow 200 – 400 mL/min (0.05 – 0.10 gal/min) Max. 0.5 bar (7.3 psi) Installation steps​ Make sure the inlet and outlet tubings are firmly attached to the online sampling device. Carefully insert the connector of the sampling device into the sampling device port on the left hand-side of the BactoSense by inserting the metallic positioning pins located inside of the sampling device connector into the openings on the BactoSense sampling device port. Tighten by hand only Then tighten the knurled fixation ring (red) until the sampling device is installed tightly. Finger-tightening only. Do not use any tools. Connect the sampling tubing safely Carefully connect the free ends of the tubings to the inlet water source and outlet drain. • Level the inlet tubing with the water source to prevent trapping of air bubbles • Shorten the length of the tubings as much as possible • Install the outlet tube with a loop in high position • Minimize the amount of connectors to reduce potential sources of contamination • To prevent any damage to the sampling device and BactoSense, make sure no force is exerted via the tubings. Fixate the tubings to a solid structure in the proximity of the sampling device (30 – 50 cm) if possible. In drinking water installations, connect the outlet tubing to a drain to make sure that the water diverted from the drinking water pipe system is not returned after flowing through the additional fittings, tubings and BactoSense sampling device. See figure 5-3. Open the water supply carefully and check the appliance for leaks. Check flow rate and pressure Adjust the flow rate coming from the water supply. Flow rate range: 200 to 400 mL/min (0.05 – 0.10 gal/min) If the flow rate is not within the specified limits, results may be inaccurate or the BactoSense may be damaged. Make sure the pressure in the sampling device does not exceed 0.5 bar (7.3 psi). Install a pressure reducer if needed. See figure 5-3.

The IO-box is an accessory to the BactoSense. It can be used to connect the in- and outputs of the BactoSense to a PLC/SCADA system. As an alternative to the I/O-Box, Modbus TCP can be used. Details can be found in Modbus TCP.
Review the specifications Carefully read the technical specifications before preparing the integration.

Use: 4 digital inputs referenced to Common allow the instrument to be controlled by an external voltage (e.g. voltage coming out of a PLC). Specifications: optocoupler input: forward voltage 1.2 VDC with 3 kΩ in serial, cathode connected to COMMON, max. 30 mA, max. 50 mW. Additional notes Digital input requirements The Common (port 18) must be connected to the reference voltage of the input voltage (e.g. 0 V / Ground of the external power source). The digital inputs (ports 14 - 17) voltage range is between 5 - 30 V to produce a logic high level or "1". Otherwise it produces a logic low level or "0". If any of the digital inputs is at a logic high level or "1", the BactoSense enters "PLC- mode".

Use: 4 digital outputs allow the reporting of 4 different logic states, e.g. errors or alarms. As the output terminals are the output of a MOS-based solid-state relay (LH1540AAB), there is no polarity. Terminals A and B can be used in either direction and can be swapped. Terminals A and B are either in high-impedance (disconnected) or low- impedance (connected) state. Specifications: freely configurable, SSR output: max. 48 VDC, max. 300 mW, ON- resistance 2 Ω.

Use: 2 analogue outputs (4 – 20 mA) allow the reporting of two analogue values, e.g. Total Cell Count and HNAP. Note: For the transmission of precise results, the use of Modbus TCP is recommended. See Modbus TCP Specifications: 2 x 0/4 – 20 mA, recommended 250 Ω load

The instrument can be controlled from an external Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). In order to avoid any conflicts when starting a process, the PLC first locks the instrument into “PLC Mode”, in which the instrument acts as a slave to the PLC. In this mode, all functions of the GUI related to running protocols and other processes are blocked. Once in PLC mode, protocols can be started and aborted from the PLC, using the Instrument’s digital inputs. The digital outputs then provide feedback to the PLC for safe operation. The PLC mode is a remote-controlled Online mode: the PLC can request a single measurement, or start the scheduler to run protocols at predefined intervals. Measurements started from the PLC also appear in the Online mode results. When no wires are connected to the digital inputs, their state is 0000. documents.t: The values of digital outputs are modified in the following situations: When the instrument is powered off, all outputs are set to 0. When the instrument is powered on, the outputs show the current error state: none / critical / non-critical. At the end of a measurement in Online mode, the outputs are changed to indicate errors and alarms, according to user-defined settings. When Reset is clicked on the output test screen or when Save is pressed on the digital output settings, the outputs are updated to show the error state only (alarms are ignored). After manually clearing the errors, the outputs are automatically reset (and therefore show the new error state and no alarms). At specific times during the measurement, extra signals can be relayed. By default, neither of them is relayed to the outputs. These are: Process running. Active when a protocol is running. Sampling device in use. Active when the sampling device is being used. It drops back to inactive after the sample preparation step of measurement protocols. Low cartridge. Active when the cartridge level is below 15 %, or if the cartridge is estimated to be empty within a month based on the current measurement frequency. Expired cartridge. Active when the cartridge is expired. The digital output state at the end of a measurement is defined according to these default values, which can be changed in the settings: If there are no errors and no alarms, all terminals are set to the user-defined base state. By default, this is 1 everywhere. In case of a critical error, the first output is set to 0. Non-critical errors set the second output to 0. Alarms set the third and fourth output to 0. In case of conflict in the output settings, priority is given to: Critical errors Non-critical errors Cartridge states Alarm Admin access required Only Admin users can change the output settings, as these can critically affect external PLC systems. The following procedure describes how to adjust the digital outputs. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings. 2. Press the Online mode settings button. 3. Press the Digital outputs button. 4. Set Base state for outputs 1–4 when no errors or alarms are active. 1: The switch is closed. 0: The switch is open. 5. Set the response of each output in the Critical error row. By default, a critical error opens output 1. 1: The switch is closed. 0: The switch is open. /: The switch is not affected by this error. 6. Set the response of each output in the Non-critical error row. By default, a non-critical error opens output 2. 7. Assign each enabled alarm to the required outputs in its alarm row. You can only assign alarms that are enabled. You can assign several alarms to the same output. Example alarm rows: High TCC (top), High HNAP (bottom). 8. Press the Save button.

The analogue current output is changed in the following situations: When the instrument is powered off, both outputs are set to 0 mA. When the instrument is powered on, both outputs are set to 2 mA. When a measurement in Online mode terminates after cell counting, the value is set between 4 and 20 mA, according to range and source definition of the analogue output settings. If the measurement fails due to an error before cell counting begins, the output remains at its previous value. When a user manually tests the output, the current is set to whatever value the user has chosen. The reset button sets them to 4 mA. Precise output values For the transmission of precise results, the use of Modbus TCP is recommended. See Modbus TCP Only Admin users can edit the analogue 4 .. 20 mA outputs. Figure 6-6 Analogue output settings 1 Output port selection 2 Source: Defines which measurement result is transmitted by this output port. 3 Lower limit 4 mA: Which value of the measurement result should correspond to 4 mA. 4 Upper limit 20 mA: Which value of the measurement result should correspond to 20 mA. 5 If selected, interpolates the chosen cell count value range with a logarithmic scale as follows: ratio = 1 + 9 × (counts − low) / (high − low) output = 4 mA + log<sub>10</sub>(ratio) × 16 mA counts: Measured cell count low: Lower cell count limit high: Higher cell count limit output: Current amplitude in mA The following procedure describes how to adjust the analogue outputs. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings. 2. Press the Online mode settings button. 3. Press the Analog outputs button. 4. Choose Port 1 or Port 2 (figure 6-6) 5. Choose the source (figure 6-6, position 2). 6. Define the lower limit of the range (figure 6-6, position 3). When the source is equal to this value, 4 mA will be output on the selected port. 7. Define the upper limit of the range (figure 6-6, position 4). When the source is equal to this value, 20 mA will be output on the selected port. 8. Press the Save button.

Log in as Admin and use Test outputs while the instrument is idle, with PLC mode disabled. Prevent unintended alarms The Test outputs interface allows to generate a physical output signal for testing purposes. Make sure that such tests do not generate an alarm on your control system. Figure 6-7 Testing analogue and digital outputs 1 Define state of digital outputs for test. 2 Set digital outputs to the state defined in (1). 3 Set all digital and analogue outputs at once. 4 Set current on both analogue outputs. 5 Reset outputs to their state before the tests. 6 Set current on port 2. 7 Set current on port 1. The following procedure describes how to test the analogue and digital outputs. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings. 2. Press the Online mode settings button. 3. Press the Test outputs button. 4. Enter the test values that you wish to send to the PLC. For digital outputs: 1: The switch is closed. 0: The switch is open. 5. Tests can be triggered individually or together (see figure 6-7): • Testing only the digital outputs on the terminals 1 – 4. • Testing only the analogue outputs on ports 1, 2 or both. • Testing all outputs. The output signals can be measured on the terminals. 6. Press the Reset button.

BactoSense maintenance refers to the activities and procedures performed to ensure the proper functioning, accuracy and reliability of the instrument over its life cycle. Follow the maintenance schedule BactoSense service duty Adhering to the maintenance schedule is important to ensure a long instrument lifetime, safe operation and correct measurement results. Service duties have to be carried out according to the maintenance schedule and original bNovate spare parts have to be used, otherwise this can lead to damage to the instrument or measurement errors. In case of neglected maintenance, bNovate Technologies accepts no warranty claims made by the customer and is not responsible for any resulting costs. Importantly, Only service-trained and authorized personnel are allowed to carry out BactoSense service operation Carry out servicing duties according to the servicing schedule in Periodic preventive maintenance by service professional and Overview of maintenance by user. When carrying out servicing duties, use original bNovate spare parts. The use of third-party spare parts requires the written approval of bNovate Technologies. If the instruments are subjected to heavy use or exposed to adverse environmental conditions, service duties must be carried out more frequently. Before maintenance Observe the safety points Before working on the instrument, ensure that you have carefully read the safety points in this user manual. You should also follow these regulations: Only professional electricians are authorized to do the electrical installation of the power plug. It is forbidden to modify or repair the BactoSense instrument. Perform the work steps in the instructed order. When replacing parts, use only genuine original parts listed in the consumables and spare parts list. When returning components use the original packaging of the BactoSense Be sure to use a plug with Protective Earth (PE) and that the device is correctly connected to it.

Preventive maintenance of the BactoSense is a scheduled intervention to replace wear parts, update the software and inspect and validate the instrument. Preventive maintenance is important to prevent failures and optimize the performance and reliability. It can only be conducted by service professionals specifically trained by bNovate. A preventive maintenance is due after the consumption of either 3 cartridges or 1 year, whichever comes first. Contact bNovate support or your local service partner to see available options. Contact details can be found in Contacting customer service.

This protocol describes how to clean the manual sampling device using the Washstation. If no Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning. This protocol automatically cleans the inner and outer surfaces of the aspiration needle. All reagents required come directly from the installed cartridge. The protocol takes approximately 15 min. Figure 15-2 Washstation for cleaning the manual sampling device WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device. 2. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 3. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 4. Select Clean Sampling Device with Washstation from the list of available protocols. 5. Make sure 1 replication is configured in the Replications column. More replications can be conducted for stronger cleanings. 6. Press the Next button. 7. Mount the Washstation by screwing it on the manual sampling device, similar to a sample tube. Make sure you install it to the end of the thread. 8. Press the Start button and wait for 15 min for the protocol to complete. 9. If the instrument will be idle or decommissioned, leave the Washstation attached to the manual sampling device. If you want to keep on measuring, remove the Washstation and close it with a cap from a 5 mL screw-cap tube. 10. If the contamination persists, repeat the procedure with more replications. If it still persists, use the Cleaning Kit to decontaminate the instrument (see Consumables).
documents.s: 15.2.2 Clean manual sampling device with Washstation

documents.t: This protocol describes how to clean the manual sampling device without the Washstation. If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation instead. This protocol requires sterile water. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device. 2. Attach a fresh 5 mL screw-cap tube containing 2 – 5 mL sterile water to the manual sampling device. 3. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 4. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 5. Select Clean Optics from the list of available protocols. 6. Make sure 1 replication is configured in the Replications column. Configure more replications for a stronger cleaning. 7. Press the Next button. 8. Press the Start button and wait for 5 min for the protocol to complete. 9. Press New to return to the protocol list, then select Clean Sampling Device. 10. Make sure 1 replication is configured in the Replications column. Configure more replications for a stronger cleaning. 11. Press the Next button. 12. Press the Start button and wait for 5 min for the protocol to complete. 13. Once the protocol is finished, remove the 5 mL screw-cap tube and discard it. 14. Press the Home icon at the top left of the user interface to return to the Home screen. 15. If you want to continue with measurements, perform a Prime prior to the first measurement. The instructions can be found in Performing a Prime. If the instrument will be idle or shut off, attach a fresh sample tube to the manual sampling device. 16. If you face a persisting contamination, first repeat the procedure with more replications. If it still persists, use the Cleaning Kit to decontaminate the instrument (see Consumables).
