documents.t: The following procedure helps clearing biological contaminations of the online sampling device. In case of persistent biological contaminations or suspected non-biological contaminations, change the online sampling device tubings as described in Replacing online sampling device tubings and contact support@bnovate.com for assistance. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the online sampling device is correctly installed and water flow conditions are fulfilled (see Installing the online sampling device at the BactoSense). Important: Make sure the outlet tubing is connected to a drain, as cleaning liquid is released into the online sampling device. 2. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 3. Select the Clean Sampling Device protocol and configure 5 replications. 4. Press Next and Start to launch the cleaning. 5. After finishing, press New to return to the protocol list. 6. Select the Prime protocol and configure 2 replications. 7. Press Next and Start to launch the priming. 8. After completion the online sampling device should be clear of minor biological contaminations and you can return to regular operation. In case contaminations persist or if a non- biological contamination is suspected, contact support@bnovate.com for assistance.

The inlet- and outlet tubings of the online sampling device must be exchanged if they show signs of damage or contamination. The required materials are the inlet and outlet tubing and two ferrules. For specifications refer to Technical data, and for the part numbers to Consumables. Do not use a spanner Never use a spanner on the sampling device when attached to the BactoSense Wear protective gloves Wear nitrile gloves when manipulating the sampling device or any other components which come in contact with the sample. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure all protocols (e.g. measurements) have terminated, or terminate them if needed. 2. Stop the water flow through the sampling device. 3. Disconnect the tubings to the water supply and drain them. 4. Carefully unscrew the knurled sampling device fixation ring until the sampling device can be removed. 5. Make sure the white sealing plug still sits tightly in the connector of the sampling device. If not, it may have remained in the BactoSense sampling device connector. In this case carefully remove it with tweezers and place it back in the sampling device. 6. Unscrew the nuts of the two connectors on the sampling device using a spanner. 7. Pull the nuts off the old tubings. 8. Discard the old tubings with ferrules. 9. Take the new tubings and install the nut and ferrule as illustrated. Screw the nut on the online sampling device using a clamp. Make sure the blue FEP tubing is connected to the top fluidic connector (see figure 5-2 in Installation of the online sampling device). 10. Continue with the procedure for installing the online sampling device described in Installing the online sampling device at the BactoSense.

The following procedure describes how to replace the desiccant bag. The desiccant bag is a consumable listed in Consumables. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Open the desiccant bag container by unscrewing the large cap on the left-hand side of the instrument. 2. Replace the used desiccant bag by a new one. 3. Close the desiccant bag container by screwing back the large cap.

The sampling device of the BactoSense contains a 25 μm filter which can be replaced by the user. The filter is a consumable listed in Consumables. Use fresh protective gloves Wear fresh, non-powdered nitrile gloves when handling the samples, sampling device, or any components which come in contact with them. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Unscrew the sampling device from the BactoSense, as described in Removal of the online sampling device for the online sampling device, and Removal of the manual sampling device for the manual sampling device. 2. Place flat tweezers under the white plug. 3. Remove the white plug and mind the transparent filter disc. The filter sometimes stays inside the cavity and sometimes remains attached to the white plug. 4. Remove the filter and place a new one. Do not use force, let the filter sink with gravity. Do not push the filter inside with tweezers. 5. Re-insert the white plug. Be sure to press it until it reaches the bottom. The force of the white plug will press the filter in the right position. 6. Re-install the sampling device as described in Installation of the manual sampling device for the manual sampling device and Installation of the online sampling device for the online sampling device.
documents.s: 15.2.7 Replacement of the sampling device filter

documents.t: Back up data before deleting When running out of disk space, old data can be deleted. Make sure you retrieve all data from other users and your data before deleting it from the BactoSense. WORK STEP 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. 3. Press Delete old measurements. This function is available to Advanced and Admin users. 4. If available, choose one of the following measuring modes: Online / Manual 5. Choose the time interval for the measurements to keep. Measurements older than this will be deleted. 6. Press Delete measurements, then confirm with Yes, delete to permanently delete the data.

Software updates can either be installed from a USB stick, or from an online repository, if an internet connection is available (e.g. through BactoLink). Software updates must be launched manually from the user interface. For updates using USB stick, contact your service partner. For updates from the online repository, follow the procedure below. WORK STEP 1. Make sure your instrument has a fast and stable internet connection and you are logged in with Admin permissions. 2. Recommended: Back up your data, e.g. using export to USB as described in Export data to USB device. 3. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. Press the Maintenance button. 4. Press System update. Available USB drives and the online repository appear in the list at the top. If no update is shown, press Refresh list. If still no update is shown, no update is available for your instrument or there is an issue with the internet connection. 5. Select the USB drive or online repository containing the desired update. 6. Carefully read through the release notes in the Changelog section of the user interface to understand the changes introduced since your current software version. 7. To update, press Update, confirm with Yes, and follow the instructions. Note: No manual reboot is necessary after the update. 8. After the update, verify that all instrument configurations are still correct.

The embedded manual lets you consult this user manual directly on the BactoSense touchscreen. Its chapters, tables, safety notices and illustrations are stored on the instrument, so no internet connection is needed to read them. The manual follows the instrument's interface language. English, German, French, Italian and Spanish are supported. If the selected language is unavailable in the installed manual, the English edition is displayed.

The manual is accessible to Basic, Advanced and Admin users. WORK STEP 1. Log in and navigate to the Home screen. 2. Press Settings. 3. Press Support & Service. 4. Under Manuals, press User manual to open the chapter contents.

Select a chapter in the contents and scroll to read it. Press a cross-reference in the text to open the corresponding section. Use the reader's toolbar to navigate and adjust the text: CONTROL FUNCTION Contents Return to the chapter list. Sections Show the headings in the current chapter. Select a heading to jump to that section, or press Read to return to the article. Search Enter a word or phrase with the on-screen keyboard and confirm the entry. Select a search result to open its location in the manual. Back Return to the previous reading position within the manual, for example after following a cross-reference. ‹ / › Open the previous or next chapter. A− / A+ Decrease or increase the text size. Press an illustration to enlarge it. Use + and − to zoom, drag to inspect details, and press Close to return to the article. Wide tables can be scrolled horizontally. To leave the manual and return to the instrument screen, press the device's Back control at the top left. External website links display an address to open on a phone or computer.

On screens with contextual help, a circled question mark appears beside the screen title. Press it to open the manual at the relevant instructions. This is useful, for example, when configuring a measurement schedule, interpreting results or changing a cartridge. Press the device's Back control at the top left to close help and return to the same screen. Your current selections and unsaved entries are retained. The embedded copy is supplied with the instrument software. To consult the online edition, press Online documentation under Manuals on the Support & Service screen and scan the QR code with a phone. Reading the online edition requires an internet connection on that device.

The BactoSense can measure manually collected grab samples using the manual sampling device, and also sample automatically from a connected water source using the online sampling device. Sample types and pretreatments: Raw waters and especially surface waters must be filtered with a 20 µm filter. Particles can block the internal filters and damage the instrument. Clear water expected to be potable usually does not need filtering. Sparkling water and soft drinks cannot be measured by the instrument. Water with a high concentration of chlorine can affect the results of the measurement. The sample and operating conditions listed in Technical data must be fulfilled.

Measuring in Online mode describes a configuration, in which the BactoSense is connected to a water source using the online sampling device, and automatically draws and measures a sample at predefined intervals. If you want to measure manually collected grab samples instead, refer to Measuring in manual mode. For different intervals or selected weekdays, see Advanced scheduling.

The following instructions show how to configure and start automatic online measurements using the online sampling device. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the online sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the online sampling device. If you have the manual sampling device installed and want to change to the online sampling device, refer to Removal of the manual sampling device to remove the manual sampling device and Installation of the online sampling device to install the online sampling device. 2. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 3. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Online mode. Press Back to return to the Home screen. 4. Press Start on the Home screen to open the online measurement wizard. 5. Under Protocol, make sure the checkbox for “Online Sampling Device (with Backflush)” is checked. 6. Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field. 7. Select the desired gate to be applied to the measurements by tapping into the Gates text field. Generally, default TCC and ICC gates are used. Use user-defined gates if your application requires it. Creating and adjusting gates is described in Results and Data Analysis. 8. Press the Next button. 9. If the weekly schedule editor is displayed, press Back to return to the simple interval schedule. Select the measurement interval using the wheel on the right hand side. The measurement interval describes the time between different measurements and can be as short as 30 min and as long as 6 hours. 10. If needed, delay the starting time by unchecking Start immediately and choosing a specific start time. The time setting of the BactoSense is described in Date and time. 11. Press the Start button. During the measurement, the current estimate of the cell concentration is displayed in the action bar under “Last”. 12. After each measurement, the time series graph is updated. For more details press the View results button. 13. If you want to stop an online measurement series, refer to Terminating automatic online measurements.
documents.s: 10.2.1 Configuring and starting automatic online measurements

documents.t: Follow the steps below to terminate a measurement series in Online mode. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. In Online mode, tap the plot on the Home screen to open the online chart. Press Stop. 2. Confirm the message to stop the Online mode measurement series. 3. If a measurement is running, you can select whether you want to abort it immediately, or wait for completion. 4. If you don’t continue with another measurement series within the next hours, proceed with removing the online sampling device as described in Removal of the online sampling device and installing the manual sampling device as described in Installation of the manual sampling device. 5. If you want to view your data, refer to Reviewing automatic online measurements. If you want to retrieve your data, refer to Data Access and Export.

In Online mode, tap the plot on the Home screen to open the line plot of the measurement results over time. Figure 10-1 Online mode results overview plot By tapping the button with a gear icon (arrow in figure 10-1), users can change the scales and which metrics are displayed (see figure 10-2). To display alarms on the plot, create an alarm and enable its "Display alarm" setting (see Alarm configuration). Figure 10-2 Online mode plot settings 1 Adjust the percentage scale. Touch the upper half of the scale bar to move the upper limit. Touch the lower half to move the lower limit. 2 Adjust the counts scale. Touch the upper half of the scale bar to move the upper limit. Touch the lower half to move the lower limit. 3 Choose the display interval or filter by name (see Filtering measurements). 4 Choose the vertical scale: • Auto scale adapts to the current data • Full scale shows the full range of the instrument • Custom scale is adjusted with sliders 1 and 2. Log and Linear control the counts scale (right-hand-side scale). 5 Choose which metrics to display on the graph.

Use advanced scheduling when measurements must run at different intervals or on selected weekdays. A weekly schedule combines one or more rules, each with its own protocol, measurement name, gates and timing. The same weekly plan repeats until you change or stop it. Advanced scheduling requires an activated Management Package or Scientific Package. If Advanced is unavailable, check the package status under Settings → System settings → Upgrades; see Upgrade Packages. Before starting, install the online sampling device and check the instrument's date and time. Create a weekly schedule​ WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Follow steps 1–8 of Configuring and starting automatic online measurements to choose Online mode, the protocol, sample name and gates. Press Next to reach the scheduling screen. 2. Press Advanced. If a weekly schedule is already configured, the rule editor may open directly. Figure 10-3 shows the Advanced control on the simple interval screen. 3. Select a rule in the left-hand list to edit it, or press New rule to add one. Select an unwanted rule and press Delete to remove it from the draft. Review the existing rules before adding another; all rules contribute to the weekly schedule. 4. Set Name, Protocol and Gate for the selected rule. Name labels the resulting measurements. Choose gates compatible with the installed cartridge. Maintenance protocols that do not need gates hide this field. 5. Choose 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, Daily or Custom. The interval presets repeat every day. Daily schedules one run per day at the chosen Start time. Use Custom to select weekdays, another interval or a time window. 6. For Custom, set Start time, select the required Days and set Interval in minutes. Press Set time range to choose the daily window, then confirm with OK. Scroll the fields below the frequency buttons to see Interval, Set time range and Range. Figures 10-4 and 10-5 show the same rule before and after scrolling. 7. Repeat steps 3–6 for any additional rules. Press Preview. Select a gate if Preview is unavailable because one is missing. If preview reports a conflict, return to the rules and adjust their times or intervals so protocols have time to finish. 8. Select each weekday in the preview and check the generated entries. Select an entry to inspect its Time, Name, Protocol and Gate. The preview can include automatically inserted cleaning protocols during long gaps. Review these alongside measurement entries; see Figure 10-6. 9. Make any individual changes described below, then press Save to apply the weekly schedule. Changes to rules and preview entries remain a draft until you press Save. 10. At Start scheduler now?, press Yes to start the saved plan, or No to save it without starting a stopped scheduler. Check the Home screen to confirm the operating state. To stop an active series, follow Terminating automatic online measurements. Figure 10-3 Open Advanced scheduling from the simple interval screen Figure 10-4 Rule editor with measurement settings, frequency and weekdays Figure 10-5 Scroll the custom fields to check the interval and time range Example: hourly monitoring on weekdays. Set Custom, Start time to 08:00, Days to Monday–Friday, Interval to 60 min and the time range to 08:00–17:00. The measurement entries start at 08:00, 09:00, …, 16:00 on those days. The range ends at 17:00; it does not add a 17:00 start. These values illustrate the controls; choose a plan appropriate for your application. For a window that crosses midnight, use separate rules for the parts before and after midnight and select the corresponding weekdays. Check the generated preview against the intended times. Adjust individual entries in the preview​ Use the preview to make an exception to the generated plan, such as moving one run or changing its measurement name. Figure 10-6 Day-by-day preview and settings for the selected entry WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Select a weekday, then an entry in the left-hand list. The fields on the right show that entry's settings. 2. Tap Time, Name, Protocol or Gate to change the selected entry. A change applies to that entry. Check the gate again if you change the protocol. A Line field is also available for protocols using BactoSwitch. 3. Press New to add an entry to the selected day, then adjust its fields. To remove an entry, select it and press Delete. Check the new entry's time, protocol and gates before saving. 4. Use Copy to week only if every day should have the same entries as the selected day. Acknowledge the confirmation with OK. This replaces the other days' entries in the draft, including weekend entries and day-specific exceptions. Review all seven days afterward. 5. Press Save, then answer Start scheduler now? as described above. If saving fails, review the message and correct the conflicting times or missing settings before retrying. Preserve individual changes Back returns from the preview to the rules. Changing a rule and generating a new preview can replace individual entry adjustments. Make those adjustments after the final rule preview and review them before saving. Change an existing schedule or return to a simple interval​ While the scheduler is running, open Home → Settings → Online mode settings → Schedule interval. Edit the weekly rules, press Preview, review the entries and press Save. If the scheduler is stopped, use Start on the Online mode Home screen to reopen the measurement wizard. To use one constant interval again, press Back from the preview to the rules, then Back to the simple interval screen. Choose the interval and confirm with OK in Schedule interval, or Start in the measurement wizard. Confirming the simple schedule replaces the advanced weekly plan; pressing Back alone does not apply the change.

Measuring in manual mode describes a configuration, in which the manual sampling device is connected to the BactoSense, and the operator attaches individual grab samples collected in 5 mL screw cap tubes to the instrument.

The following instructions show how to configure and start a measurement in manual mode. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device. 2. If the manual sampling device has been newly installed or the instrument has been switched off or idle for more than 3 days, it is recommended to clean the sampling device. If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation, otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning. 3. If a cleaning of the manual sampling device has been conducted (see previous step), it is recommended to perform a prime prior to measuring the sample. Follow the procedure in Performing a Prime. 4. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 5. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 6. Select Water Analysis from the list of available protocols. If you want technical replicates, select the number of replicates in Replications column. By default, one sample is measured. If more replicates are configured, multiple samples are drawn from the same sample tube. 7. Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field, entering the name and pressing OK. 8. Check whether your desired gate is configured in the Gates field. If you wish to use another gate, tap into the Gates field and select the desired gate from the available options (depending on the cartridge installed). Generally, default TCC and ICC gates are used. Use user-defined gates if your application requires it. Creating and adjusting gates is described in Results and Data Analysis. 9. Press the Next button. 10. Attach a 5 mL screw-cap tube containing 2 – 5 mL of sample to the manual sampling device. 11. Press the Start button. The estimated protocol duration and expected termination timepoint are displayed. The current state of the measurement is indicated in the top bar (e.g. Initializing, Mixing...) 12. After finishing the measurement, press Next to view the results. Results are explained in Measurement results. 13. If you want to proceed with the next measurement, press the New button. 14. If you want to see previous measurement results, press the View results button. 15. If you want to rename, regate or export the measurement, refer to the instructions in following sections. 16. If you don’t want to measure more samples and the instrument will be idle or switched off, perform a cleaning of the manual sampling device. If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation, otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning.
documents.s: 10.3.1 Performing a measurement in manual mode

documents.t: Measurements can be renamed from their result details view. WORK STEP 1. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode). 2. In the results list, select the measurement you want to rename. Exception: If you want to rename a group of replicates (see Working with measurement replicates), long- press on the group of replicates and then press the rename button. 3. In the result details view, press the Rename button (see Measurement results). 4. A keyboard and text field with the current sample name will appear. Use the keyboard to change the sample name and press OK.

When working in manual mode, analysis protocols can be repeated. This is particularly useful for generating technical replicates of a single sample. The number of replicates can be selected when configuring a manual measurement, as described in Performing a measurement in manual mode. In the manual mode results list, replicates are grouped into one entry, and the number in brackets next to the sample name indicates the number of replicates. In this view, the results shown for the replicate group consist of average and standard deviation. Individual replicate measurements can be accessed by pressing on the replicate group. Replicate groups can easily be renamed, deleted, exported or regated after a long-press on the replicate group in the manual mode results list.
Adjusting the gates of individual measurements or a set of measurements is described in Change gates.

Filtering can be applied to display a subset of the measurement results. Filtering by text and date range is possible. WORK STEP 1. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode). 2. In the results list, press the Filter button. 3. Specify your filter by applying one or both of the following options: • Define a date range by specifying start and end date • Define a text string to filter by measurement name 4. Press OK. The result list will be refreshed showing filtered results.

There are multiple ways to retrieve measurement data. Retrieval via HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and the web interface are described in Data Access and Export and Web User Interface. In this section, data export to a USB drive is described.

It is possible to export selected or all measurements to a USB flash drive. Make sure your USB flash drive is formatted in FAT32 format. WORK STEP 1. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode). 2. In the results list: • Press Export series, choose the date range and optional name filter, then press OK to export a series. • Long-press a replicate group, then press Export to export that group. • Open a single measurement, then press Export to export only that measurement. 3. In the folder name field, the name of the target folder which will be created on the USB drive is shown. Change the name if desired. 4. Insert a USB stick with enough available memory. Press Refresh list to display the connected USB stick. 5. Export options • press Export results to export only the basic results (see details in the user interface) • press Export all to export results, raw data and diagnostic information (see details in the user interface) 6. Wait for the export to complete and then press OK.

Operators can choose between two analysis protocols in manual mode. Table 10-1 Analysis protocols for manual mode PROTOCOL NAME PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION Water Analysis Analyze a water sample and finish with a cleaning cycle. If several replications are executed, the cleaning step is executed only once, at the end. A prime is executed automatically between replicates. Beads Analysis This protocol is intended for the analysis of calibration beads and is used with the Validation Kit. The protocol automatically finishes with a cleaning cycle. If several replications are executed, the cleaning step is executed only once, at the end. Maintenance protocols can be executed before or between analysis protocols, to prepare, flush, or clean the system. In manual mode, the following maintenance protocols are available: Table 10-2 Maintenance protocols for manual mode PROTOCOL NAME PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION Clean Optics Launches a cleaning step that washes all components in contact with the sample inside the BactoSense, except the sampling device. Clean Sampling Device with Washstation Cleans the manual sampling device such that the outside filter, the needle's interior and exterior can be fully washed between measurements, after a dirty sample or in case of filter blockage. The Washstation device must be mounted on the manual sampling device and a cartridge must be installed for this protocol to appear. This protocol has a higher disinfection power than the Clean Sampling Device protocol and should therefore be preferred. Using the Washstation is the best way to keep the manual sampling device clean and to avoid cross- contaminations. Instructions for this protocol can be found in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation. Clean Sampling Device Cleans the sampling device so that the external filter and the needle’s interior can be washed after an extremely loaded sample or in case of filter blockage. Instructions for this protocol can be found in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning. Fill Tubing Fills all tubing carrying reagents from the cartridge, to remove bubbles in the tubing. Cleans optics at the end of the process. Prime and Clean Optics Fills the tubing with liquid from the sample. Helps to dilute any residues after a clean sampling device for instance. Is finished by the cleaning step. Prime Loads sample into the instrument. Instructions can be found in Performing a Prime.

documents.t: Operators can choose between two analysis protocols in Online mode. Table 10-3 Analysis protocols for Online mode PROTOCOL NAME PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION Online Sampling Device (with Backflush) This is the standard protocol to be used with the online sampling device. This protocol includes automated cleaning procedures between measurements. Manual Sampling Device This protocol is used with the manual sampling device installed.
documents.s: 10.9.2 Overview of protocols in Online mode

documents.t: Priming preconditions the BactoSense with the sample. Priming can be used to reduce the carryover of cells or unwanted substances, and takes approximately 5 minutes. Use a Prime under the following circumstances: After a Clean Sampling Device protocol (with and without Washstation) After measuring a sample with a high chlorine concentration or any other unwanted substance which may affect subsequent measurements WORK STEP 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device. 2. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 3. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 4. Select Prime from the list of available protocols. 5. Press the Next button. 6. Attach the sample you want to measure next to the manual sampling device. 7. Press the Start button.

The figure below shows the result of a selected TCC measurement in Online mode. From here, the user can delete or rename the measurement, look up older results (and export them), or export the result. Expert users can repeat the cell counting with new gates. Some user interface elements or actions are only available to specific user roles (Basic, Advanced or Admin). Figure 11-1 Display of a TCC measurement result in Online mode. 1 Main result parameters, depending on cartridge type used. Find more information in Cartridges, gates and result parameters. Tap the information icon beside the main result to display all result parameters (2). 2 Result information window with all available result parameters and the main dotplot. 3 Main dotplot in the result information window. The FL1 vs FL2 dotplot shows all detected events according to the amplitude of their fluorescence signals FL1 (535 nm, X-axis) and FL2 (715 nm, Y-axis). The red polygon and vertical line show the configured gate. For details refer to Cartridges, gates and result parameters. Tap this dotplot preview to open a pop-up with access to all dotplots (4). 4 Pop-up window with access to all dotplots. The FL1 vs SSC dotplot shows only cells inside the FL1 - FL2 polygon gate, according to their fluorescence signal FL1 (535 nm) and scattered light signal SSC (488 nm). The FL1 histogram shows all cells inside the FL1 - FL2 polygon gate, binned according to their fluorescence in FL1. The available dotplots depend on your instrument model and configuration. 5 The measurement status field indicates alarms or warnings. Tap an alarm or warning indication to view its details. 6 The Delete button removes the measurement permanently (requires confirmation). 7 The Rename button can be used to change the measurement name. 8 The Re-gate result button allows to apply a different gating to the measurement data. For details refer to Regate measurements. 9 The Export button allows to save this result to a USB stick. More information can be found in Export to a USB drive. 10 The navigation buttons on the left and right of the result view allow you to navigate to the previous and next measurements, respectively. 11 Touch the trend plot to open the Auto mode plot (the full Online results chart). See Reviewing automatic online measurements. Select multiple measurements Multiple selection & batch operations: In the list of measurements, long-press on one measurement to activate the selection of multiple measurements, then select Delete / Re-gate or Export.

Following flow cytometry standards, the BactoSense uses gates to count cells in samples. We define: Gate: A line or polygon applied to a dotplot to quantify populations of measured cells. Set of gates, or gating set: A collection of two or more gates, used for the gating strategy. The types of gates are fixed, but users can change the limits of each gate. These are different for TCC and ICC measurements. Gating strategy: Defines how the gates are combined to count cells. For example, HNAC is the number of cells that are inside the TCC polygon and higher than the HNA lower limit. These strategies are different for TCC and ICC measurements. Gating sets are specific for a type of cartridge. As an example, only gating sets of type TCC can be used with measurements performed using a TCC cartridge.

The BactoSense has preconfigured gating sets for all available cartridge types. These gating sets are called Default gating sets. They have been carefully designed to be applicable to the vast majority of samples. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Gate settings to view the available gating sets. Default gating sets can neither be modified nor deleted. New gating sets can be created by editing a copy of an existing gating set, as described in Create a new gating set.

On the Home screen, press Settings, then Gate settings to view the available gating sets. Figure 11-2 List of available gating sets and options to copy and create new sets. This gating set contains an additional configurable polygon gate. Note: For some instrument models, an additional feature is needed for using the additional gate (see Scientific package). 4 Gate types, to be used with the respective cartridge type. 5 Delete an existing gating set. Default gates can not be deleted. 6 Preview the gating set. 7 Create a copy of the gating set. 8 Edit the gating set. Default gates can not be edited. 9 Create a new gating set.

documents.t: Depending on the cartridge used for a measurement, different parameters are measured. The subsections below describe gating sets and result parameters for TCC (Total Cell Count), ICC (Intact Cell Count), ACC (Active Cell Count), CBC (Coliform Cell Count), EBC (E. coli Cell Count), and NBC (Enterococcus Cell Count). CBC, EBC and NBC cartridges are compatible with BactoSense ID and BactoSense SMART. Each uses selective enzymatic labelling and a single polygon gate, and reports one cell concentration. No HNA or activity subpopulations are calculated for these cartridges. Interpreting CBC, EBC and NBC results CBC, EBC and NBC are cell concentrations expressed in cells per millilitre (1/mL). Cell counts and culture results expressed in colony-forming units (CFU) measure different properties of a sample and cannot be compared directly.

TCC refers to Total Cell Count. The TCC cartridge is therefore used to measure the concentration of all cells. Table 11-1 Gating set used for the TCC cartridge. GATE TYPE DESCRIPTION TCC Polygon A polygon defined on the FL1-FL2 plane. Points inside this polygon are counted as cells (TCC). HNA lower limit Vertical line A threshold on FL1. Points within TCC but larger than the HNA lower limit in FL1 are counted as HNAC. Points within TCC but smaller than the limit are counted as LNAC. Table 11-2 Result parameters obtained from the TCC cartridge. PARAMETER UNIT NAME DESCRIPTION TCC 1/mL Total Cell Count Total number of cells detected inside the TCC gate. It is an addition of HNAC and LNAC: TCC = HNAC + LNAC HNAP % High Nucleic Acid Percentage The percentage of HNA cells relative to TCC: HNAP = (HNAC / TCC) × 100 LNAC 1/mL Low Nucleic Acid Count The number of cells inside the TCC gate, but below the HNA lower limit (vertical line gate). HNAC 1/mL High Nucleic Acid Count The number of cells inside the TCC gate and above the HNA lower limit (vertical line gate). For further information on how to adjust the gates see Change gates.

ICC refers to Intact Cell Count. The ICC cartridge is therefore used to measure the concentration of intact cells. Table 11-3 Gating set used for the ICC cartridge. GATE TYPE DESCRIPTION ICC Polygon A polygon defined on the FL1-FL2 plane. Points inside this polygon are counted as intact cells (ICC). HNA lower limit Vertical line A threshold on FL1. Points within ICC but larger than the HNA lower limit in FL1 are counted as HNAC. Points within ICC but smaller than the limit are counted as LNAC. Table 11-4 Result parameters obtained from the ICC cartridge. PARAMETER UNIT NAME DESCRIPTION ICC 1/mL Intact Cell Count Total number of intact cells inside the ICC gate: ICC = HNAC + LNAC HNAP % High Nucleic Acid Percentage The percentage of HNA cells relative to ICC: HNAP = (HNAC / ICC) × 100 LNAC 1/mL Low Nucleic Acid Count The number of LNA cells inside the ICC gate, but below the HNA lower limit (vertical line gate). HNAC 1/mL High Nucleic Acid Count The number of HNA cells inside the ICC gate and above the HNA lower limit (vertical line gate). For further information on how to adjust the gates see Change gates.

ACC refers to Active Cell Count. The ACC cartridge is therefore used to measure the concentration of metabolically active cells, using an enzymatic assay. Table 11-5 Gating set used for the ACC cartridge. GATE TYPE DESCRIPTION ACC Polygon A polygon defined on the FL1-FL2 plane. Points inside this polygon are counted as active cells (ACC). HACC lower limit Vertical line A threshold on FL1. Points within ACC but larger than the HACC lower limit in FL1 are counted as HACC. Points within ACC but smaller than the limit are counted as LACC. Table 11-6 Result parameters obtained from the ACC cartridge. PARAMETER UNIT NAME DESCRIPTION ACC 1/mL Active Cell Count Total number of active cells inside the ACC gate: ACC = HACC + LACC HACC 1/mL Highly Active Cell Count The number of active cells with FL1 intensity higher than the HACC vertical gate. LACC 1/mL Lowly Active Cell Count The number of active cells with FL1 intensity lower than the HACC vertical gate. HACP % Highly Active Cell Percentage The percentage of HACC among ACC. HACP = (HACC / ACC) × 100 For further information on how to adjust the gates see Change gates.

CBC refers to Coliform Cell Count. The CBC cartridge measures the concentration of coliform bacteria using an enzymatic assay based on β-galactosidase activity. The enzyme converts the cartridge substrate into a fluorescent product, enabling detection of the labelled cells by flow cytometry. Table 11-7 Gating set used for the CBC cartridge. GATE TYPE DESCRIPTION CBC Polygon A polygon defined on the FL1-FL2 plane. Fluorescently labelled coliform cells inside this polygon contribute to CBC. Table 11-8 Result parameter obtained from the CBC cartridge. PARAMETER UNIT NAME DESCRIPTION CBC 1/mL Coliform Cell Count Concentration of labelled coliform cells inside the CBC gate, calculated from the cell count and analysed sample volume. For further information on how to adjust the gates see Change gates.

EBC refers to E. coli Cell Count. The EBC cartridge measures the concentration of Escherichia coli bacteria using an enzymatic assay based on β-glucuronidase activity. The enzyme converts the cartridge substrate into a fluorescent product, enabling detection of the labelled cells by flow cytometry. Table 11-9 Gating set used for the EBC cartridge. GATE TYPE DESCRIPTION EBC Polygon A polygon defined on the FL1-FL2 plane. Fluorescently labelled E. coli cells inside this polygon contribute to EBC. Table 11-10 Result parameter obtained from the EBC cartridge. PARAMETER UNIT NAME DESCRIPTION EBC 1/mL E. coli Cell Count Concentration of labelled E. coli cells inside the EBC gate, calculated from the cell count and analysed sample volume. For further information on how to adjust the gates see Change gates.

NBC refers to Enterococcus Cell Count. The NBC cartridge measures the concentration of enterococci using an enzymatic assay based on β-glucosidase activity. The enzyme converts the cartridge substrate into a fluorescent product, enabling detection of the labelled cells by flow cytometry. Table 11-11 Gating set used for the NBC cartridge. GATE TYPE DESCRIPTION NBC Polygon A polygon defined on the FL1-FL2 plane. Fluorescently labelled enterococci inside this polygon contribute to NBC. Table 11-12 Result parameter obtained from the NBC cartridge. PARAMETER UNIT NAME DESCRIPTION NBC 1/mL Enterococcus Cell Count Concentration of labelled enterococci inside the NBC gate, calculated from the cell count and analysed sample volume. For further information on how to adjust the gates see Change gates.

Regating is the process of applying a different gating set to existing measurement data. A prerequisite for regating is the presence of such additional gating set. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Gate settings to view the available gating sets. The process of modifying an existing gating set is described in Edit existing gating sets. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 2. Press Logs, then Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode), depending on how the measurement was performed. 3. To regate a single measurement, select the measurement to see the result details page. To regate multiple measurements (batch), long-press on the measurement, until it is highlighted and a check box appears on the left. Then tap on more measurement to also select them for regating. 4. Press Re-gate result in the single-result view, or Re-gate when several measurements are selected. 5. Select the desired gating set by checking its box. 6. Press the Confirm button to start the regating process. Additional information Depending on the number of measurements, regating can take several minutes. 7. After finishing, press OK.

New gating sets can be created either from a copy of an existing gating set, or from scratch. Creating a new gating set from a copy WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Gate settings button. 3. In the list of available gating sets, identify the gating set from which you want to make a copy to create the new gating set. Make sure the gating type (e.g. TCC, ICC) matches with your target application. 4. Press the Copy icon to create a copy of the gating set. 5. In the newly generated copy, press the Edit icon and follow the editing instructions in Edit existing gating sets. Creating a new gating set from scratch WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Gate settings button. 3. In the action bar at the bottom, press New. 4. Enter a name for the set of gates and select one of the available templates for the installed cartridge. 5. Then follow the gate configuration on- screen wizard as describe in the gate editing instructions in Edit existing gating sets. 6. After finishing, you can select the new gating set when creating new measurements, or regate existing measurements, as described in Regate measurements.

Apart from default gating sets, all other gating sets can be modified. Gate editing can comprise renaming, changing the position of the vertical gate, and changing the number and position of the corners of the polygon gate. In this section, the general process of editing a gating set is described. Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC describes a specific strategy to adjust gating sets for TCC and ICC measurements. Figure 11-3 Gate settings for TCC ① Coordinates of the gate’s points. a: First point in the gate b: Second point in the gate c: Third point in the gate d: Fourth point in the gate ② Remove a point from the gate. ③ Add a new point to the gate. ④ Modify the selected coordinate. In this screenshot, the FL1 (a, FL1) coordinate of the first point is selected, so we can move the first point in the gate along the FL1 axis (X-axis). ⑤ HNA lower limit: this gate is defined on the next screen. ⑥ Preview The following procedure describes how to adjust a gate: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Gate settings button. 3. Press the Edit button of the gate you wish to edit. 4. Change the name if desired, then press the Next button. 5. Adjust the number and position of polygon corners (for TCC and ICC refer to Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC). A polygon gate can have between 3 and 6 corners. 6. Press the Next button. 7. Enter the HNA lower limit (for TCC and ICC refer to Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC). 8. Press Save. In the save dialog, choose Save to update the existing set, or Save as new set to keep the original and create a new set. 9. After finishing, you can select the modified gating set when creating new measurements, or regate existing measurements, as described in Regate measurements.

The BactoSense is delivered with default gate sets that are suitable for the vast majority of samples. If needed however, advanced users have the possibility to adjust the gate. A general procedure to adjust the gate is explained below and is valid for both TCC and ICC cartridges. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Measure a water sample using the standard Water analysis protocol. On the Result details page, the FL1 vs FL2 dotplot shows: 1) LNA and HNA cells in the water 2) Electrical noise from the optical detectors 3) Debris/background noise (This can include damaged cells, aggregates or other particles) 2. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. Press the Gate settings button. 3. Depending on your needs, perform one of the following: • Create a new set of gates • Edit an existing set of gates • Copy an existing set of gates and edit the copy 4. Give a name to this set of gates and press Next. 5. Place the polygon gate at each extremity (left and right). For example, use these four points: FL1 FL2 3.0 0.0 3.0 6.1 6.5 6.1 6.5 0.0 6. Press Next and Save. For a new template, confirm with Yes. For an edited set, choose Save or Save as new set in the save dialog. 7. Navigate to the result view of the water sample you measured previously. 8. On the result view, press the Re-gate result button. 9. Select the gate you just created, and re- process the data with the new gate by pressing the button Confirm. 10. Open the FL1 histogram and locate the first valley after the noise peak, i.e. the first minimum after the peak at the extreme left (arrow in the picture). Write down the FL1 value of this minimum (e.g. 3.8). 11. Return to Gate settings and again edit your gate. Place the left limits of the gate at the previously determined FL1 value. This will exclude the electrical noise of the optical detectors. If needed, for the FL2 axis, place the points “b” and “c” of the gate just below the debris/background area (generally appearing as straight diagonals). 12. Save the adjusted gate. 13. Navigate again to the result view of the water sample you measured previously. 14. On the result view, press the Re-gate result button. 15. Select the gate you just created, and re- process the data with the new gate by pressing the button Confirm. 16. To place the HNA lower limit, open again the FL1 histogram and locate the minimum between the LNA and HNA peaks (vertical line on the image). Write down its FL1 value (e.g. 4.8). 17. Return to Gate settings and again edit your gate. 18. Navigate to the HNA lower limit configuration step. Enter the previously identified HNA lower limit to the FL1 field, press Save and select Save in the save dialog. 19. Regate the water analysis measurement again and verify that the gate is suitable. Further adjust if needed.

documents.t: BactoSense measurement data can be exported in Flow Cytometry Standard (FCS) 3.1 file format. The FCS file format is standardized by the International Society for Advancement of Cytometry (ISAC) to ensure interoperability between different flow cytometry instruments and analysis software. There are different versions of the FCS format with each version introducing improvements and additional features. FCS data can be used for custom offline postprocessing, such as the application of complex gating strategies, “microbial fingerprinting”, automated anomaly detection and many more.

FCS files can be retrieved in the following ways: Download to a USB stick: Using the Export all function (see Export settings, diagnostics, or all to USB device) Download from the web interface, either as single files (see Download an FCS-file) or multiple files (see Download a zip file with multiple results) Access using FTP (see Retrieve data via FTP) Access using HTTPS (see Retrieve files via HTTP or HTTPS) For help with the setup of an advanced data analysis tool chain, please contact support@bnovate.com.

To compare results of the BactoSense to another flow cytometer, a reference solution containing auto fluorescent beads can be analyzed. This method allows the user to compare the measurement scales of different devices. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. It is recommended to use the Validation Kit which contains a ready to use beads solution. Read the instructions of the Validation Kit for more information. 2. Install the manual sampling device according to the user manual. 3. Take of one of the Validation kit’s beads solutions and load it into the sampling device. Read the instructions of the Validation Kit for more information. 4. Additional information Press the Home button. Press the Back button as many times as needed for the Home button to appear. 5. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 6. Select Prime from the protocol list. See Performing a Prime. 7. Press the Next and Start button. Let the priming protocol finish. 8. Press New, choose Beads Analysis from the list, then press Next and Start. 9. Wait for the results and if necessary, precisely adjust the gate of the FL1 vs FL2 dot plot to count only the 4 populations of beads. It is important to ensure that noise, background, and debris are not counted into the gate. See Edit existing gating sets to adjust the gate. 10. On the FL1 vs counts histogram, estimate the log value of each peak’s center on the FL1 axis. In this example, we obtain approximately (in log): 1st peak = 4.05 2nd peak = 4.3 3rd peak = 5.35 4th peak = 6.2 11. Measure the same beads with the other flow cytometer you want to compare and repeat the steps 10 and 11. In this example, we obtain approximately (in log): 1st peak = log(103) = 3 2nd peak = log(2103) = 3.3 3rd peak = log(2.4104) = 4.4 4th peak = log(1.6*105) = 5.2 12. With the different values obtained for both devices, it is now possible to compare their scales and their measurement windows.

Damaged cables Damaged instrument or cabling Touching damaged cables may lead to electrical shocks or death. The instrument may be operated only when the cables are intact. The instrument may be operated only if it has been properly installed or repaired. Mains voltage Dangerous voltage inside the supplied mains device Touching a wet or damaged mains device may lead to electrical shocks or death. Do not position the mains device in moist locations. Do not operate the mains device if its housing is damaged. Correct supply voltage Damage due to incorrect service voltage If the instrument is connected to an incorrect service voltage, the instrument can be damaged. The instrument must only be connected to voltage sources as specified on the type plate. The instrument must only be operated with the supplied power supply unit, as described in Connecting the BactoSense to power. Keep the manual available Missing user manual Operating the instrument without following the procedures indicated in the user manual may lead to injuries to persons and damage to the instrument. If the instrument changes hands, always include the user manual. If the user manual is lost, you can contact bNovate to request a replacement at www.bnovate.com/contact. Prevent condensation Moisture or condensation on the electrical components If moisture enters the instrument, the BactoSense can be damaged. The covers and lids must always be attached during operation. Service inside the instrument must only be performed by trained personnel in a dry room and at room temperature. The instrument should be at operating or room temperature (avoid condensation on optical and electrical surfaces). Avoid aggressive chemicals Use of aggressive chemicals Use of aggressive chemicals can cause damage to instrument components. Do not use aggressive chemicals or cleaning agents. Should the instrument come in contact with aggressive chemicals, clean it thoroughly with a neutral cleaning agent. Use a damp cloth (water only) to clean the exterior of the device.

Handle chemicals safely Improper handling of chemicals Please observe the following instructions for safe handling of chemicals: Wear the recommended personal protection (safety goggles, protective gloves, protective clothing). Wash your hands thoroughly after working with chemicals. Study the MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet) before working with chemicals. If an accidental release happens, please follow the instructions of the MSDS. Never smoke or store food or beverages in the working environment.

Measurement accuracy Residual risk According to the risk assessment of the applied safety directive DIN EN 61010-1, there remains the risk of the displayed measurement values being incorrect. This risk can be reduced with the following measures: Use an access code to prevent unauthorized persons from changing parameters. Perform the specified servicing duties.

Follow the safety instructions No warning or danger symbols on the instrument Users must ensure that they observe the safety measures as specified in the user manual at all times when working with the instrument and its peripheral equipment, even if no warning or danger symbols are attached to the instrument. Observe safety points when performing the described procedures. Observe local safety regulations.

documents.t: Protect network access BactoSense is equipped with an integrated web user interface. If directly connected to the internet without appropriate protection, unauthorized internet users can access your instrument. Please follow these recommendations: Never expose the instrument’s network ports unprotected to the internet. Operate it behind a firewall and block access to the instrument. Connect to branch offices only via VPN. Change the standard password on commissioning. Always keep up-to-date with the latest changes regarding internet security. Immediately install the latest updates (also for the router and firewall).

The Scientific Package is intended for water research professionals to perform advanced data analysis. It contains the following features: Additional gate: Apply an additional configurable polygon gate to the FL1 / FL2 data directly in the user interface. Light scattering data: Record and display forward and side scatter data for each detected event. Retrieve data in FCS files for post-processing. Additional polygon gate The freely configurable additional polygon gate has the following properties: It is available for TCC and ICC cartridges. The result parameter is a cell concentration named “Gate+”. The gate can be adjusted similar to the TCC or ICC default gates. Please refer to Change gates. Forward and side scatter detector The Forward Scatter (FSC) detector measures light that is scattered by bacteria or other particles. The detector is placed at a small angle to the laser beam’s direction, thus measuring light signals in “forward” direction. In contrast, the Side Scatter (SSC) detector is placed at 90 degrees from the beam’s direction, measuring light scattered towards the side. The combination of fluorescence and scattering information provides high content data, enabling applications like microbiological fingerprinting, profiling or anomaly detection. Scattering data is available in the following ways: in the flow cytometry standard (FCS) files. For more information about this file format please refer to Advanced data analysis. on the BactoSense user interface as a FSC / SSC dotplot on the web interface as a FSC / SSC dotplot when downloading the dotplots as images Activation of the Scientific Package Activate the package while the instrument is idle, with PLC mode and Demo mode disabled. If the instrument encounters a problem, it enters a different state, depending on the severity of the issue. There are warnings, noncritical errors and critical errors, each having different implications and requiring different actions.

Warnings appear when unusual behaviour is detected during an otherwise successful measurement. They can indicate reduced accuracy of the measurement results or indicate impending errors. Unlike errors, warnings do not prevent the instrument from functioning, but users should pay attention to them as they can indicate sources of inaccuracies. WARNING IMAGE When unusual behavior is detected, a warning is shown next to the measurement results. More information on the warning can be found by clicking on the corresponding warning entry next to the measurement results or directly in the warning log. The following warning messages can be displayed: Table 16-1 Warnings ERROR CODE NAME DESCRIPTION CAUSES / WHAT TO DO W01 Cartridge expired Cartridge reagents have expired. Measurement accuracy could be affected. • Please replace the cartridge as soon as possible. W02-04 High baseline signal in FL1 / FL2 / SSC Baseline signals are too high. This is usually due to bubbles or particles in suspension in the sample. Measurement accuracy could be affected. • Check the inlet tubing for any signs of deposits. • Check the water connections, be sure that they are all tight (no air entry). • If the warning persists, please perform cleaning of instrument with the cleaning kit. W05 Incubator temperature off target Temperature during incubation was more than 2 °C off target. Cell counts may be affected. The incubator may be defective. • If the problem persists, please contact customer service. W06 No events detected No events detected during the measurement. • If the problem persists, please contact customer service. W07 TCC out of range TCC is above the specification limit of BactoSense of 2’000’000 cells/ml. • Please dilute the sample to ensure accuracy of the measurement. W08 Air bubbles detected The sample appears to contain air bubbles. • Check sampling device is installed properly. • Check the sample for bubbles. • If using online sampling device, check water is supplied at correct pressure. W10 Enclosure too cold Enclosure is too cold, rapid heating has been activated before continuing protocol. • Instrument cannot safely operate if internal temperature is too cold. • Rapid heating attempts to heat the enclosure to ensure safe operations. • Measurements will start once internal temperature is sufficient. W11 Service required Service of the instrument is required. Measurement precision can no longer be guaranteed. Continued operation can lead to leaks, which can damage the instrument. • Next service date is overdue. • Valve and plunger have reached end of life. • Please contact your service representative. W13 Laser end of life Laser has reached end of life. • Please contact your service representative. W14 Non-critical power cut The instrument was powered off unexpectedly. • Ensure the cleanliness of the instrument. • If the issue occurs frequently, install an uninterruptible power supply

Non-critical errors prevent a measurement from terminating successfully, but do not prevent the instrument from running another measurement afterwards. These errors do not require human intervention. Some non-critical errors are promoted to critical errors if they repeat three times. NON-CRITICAL ERRORS The protocol stops. The cause of the error is usually fixed by repeating the analysis or waiting. • Another measurement can immediately be started. If it completes successfully, the error state is cleared. • More information on the error can be found in the error log, by clicking on the corresponding error entry. The following non-critical error messages can be displayed: Table 16-2 List of non-critical errors. E08 Enclosure too damp Enclosure humidity is too high for safe operation. • Replace desiccant bag, by unscrewing the large cap on the left-hand-side of the instrument (see Replacement of the desiccant bag). • If the problem persists, please contact customer service. E14 Laser too hot Laser temperature is too high for safe operation. • Reduce ambient temperature or increase measurement interval to allow instrument to cool down. E18 Pump underpressure error Underpressure detected during dispense. • Missing sample. • Air in the input. • Leak in the system. • Please execute the Clean Optics protocol (see Overview of protocols in manual mode). E19 System overheated The inner temperature is too high for operation. • Reduce ambient temperature, or increase measurement interval to allow instrument to cool down. E33 Processing memory overflow Signal processing circuits memory has overflown. • Please execute the Clean Optics protocol (see Overview of protocols in manual mode). • Retry the measurement. This can be caused by a too elevated bacterial content in the water or turbidity/debris. • The accuracy of the measurement is probably very low. Repeat the measurement while diluting the sample with clear water. E46 Cartridge is still busy The cartridge was still initializing when the measurement started. • Non-critical error. Repeat the measurement. If the problem persists, contact a service technician. If the problem persists, contact a service technician. E49 GPIO Timeout error The processing board is waiting for another module to respond. • Non-critical error. Repeat the measurement. If the problem persists, contact a service technician. E50 Pump motion blocked The motion of the pump is blocked. • Non-critical error. Repeat the measurement. If the problem persists, contact a service technician. E51 Unable to get temperature reading Unable to get temperature reading. The control loop is thus disabled. • Non-critical error. Repeat the measurement. If the problem persists, contact a service technician. E52 Cartridge valve motion blocked The motion of the cartridge valve is blocked. • Non-critical error. Repeat the measurement. If the problem persists, contact customer service. E55 M7 not connected The acquisition processor cannot be initialized. • Reboot the instrument. • If the problem persists, contact customer service. E56 Empty acquisition No events detected during acquisition • Clean the sampling device using the Washstation, then perform a measurement of clean water. • If the problem persists, contact customer service. E57 Cartridge busy (special command busy) Communication with the cartridge failed. • Non-critical error. Repeat the measurement. • If the problem persists, contact customer service. Critical errors interrupt the workflows of the instrument and require human intervention. The error source needs to be eliminated and the instrument set to running conditions again. Critical errors need to be cleared. CRITICAL ERRORS IMAGE If a critical error occurs during operation, it has the following effects: • The protocol immediately stops. • The instrument goes into a critical error state, and manual intervention is needed before any new protocol can be launched. • The cause of the error must be solved by an operator. The errors can then be manually cleared from the Error log, as described in Error and warning logs and Clearing errors. The following critical error messages can be displayed: Table 16-3 List of critical errors. ERROR CODE NAME DESCRIPTION CAUSES / WHAT TO DO E00 General error Unhandled error. • Please contact customer service E02 Cartridge empty Cartridge is empty. • Replace cartridge (see Change cartridges) E04 Cartridge missing Cartridge is missing. • Insert a cartridge (see Installing a cartridge) E05 Full waste bag Cartridge waste bag is full. • Replace cartridge (see Change cartridges) E06 Cartridge communication impossible Cartridge is disconnected, door is open, or cartridge electronics are damaged. • Make sure the cartridge’s electronic cable is connected properly, and that the door is properly closed. • If that doesn’t help, replace the cartridge and inform customer service. E07 Storage disk full Insufficient storage space to continue operation. • Delete old measurements and try again (see Clearing of disk space) • This will delete the measurements permanently from the device. • Export measurements as backup solution. E12 FPGA initialization error Failed to initialize the signal processing chip. • Reboot the instrument. E16 Processing error An error was discovered while processing the signals. • The accuracy of the latest result is not guaranteed. Please repeat the analysis. E17 Overpressure detected Overpressure detected during dispense. • Likely cause: The output filter is probably clogged. • Optical flow cell blocked. • Please call customer service. E20 Abnormal shutdown Protocol interrupted for unknown reasons, usually due to a power cut. • Usually indicates a power cut, or other external interruption to the measurement. • Perform a Clean Optics and Clean Sampling Device protocol before starting a new measurement (see Overview of protocols in manual mode). E23 Temperature Sensor Communication Error Communication with temperature sensor on IO board failed. • Please contact customer service. E24 Laser Communication Error Communication with optical unit failed. • Please contact customer service. E25 Pump Communication Error Communication with pump module impossible. • Please contact customer service. E26 Power Supply Communication Error Communication with power supply module impossible. • Please contact customer service. E27 Pump Communication timeout Communication with pump module timed out. • The cartridge door is open. • A cable is disconnected. • A circuit board is damaged, either in the pump or cartridge. E28 Empty dye supply Dye tube connected to cartridge is empty. • The tube is disconnected. • Cartridge is defective. • Repeat the cartridge change procedure, making sure that all tubes are properly connected. E29 Empty rinse fluid supply Rinse fluid tube connected to cartridge is empty. • The tube is disconnected. • Cartridge is defective. • Repeat the cartridge change procedure, making sure that all tubes are properly connected. E30 Empty bleach supply Bleach tube connected to cartridge is empty • The tube is disconnected. • Cartridge is defective. • Repeat the cartridge change procedure, making sure that all tubes are properly connected. E31 Cartridge electronics failure Cartridge level can no longer be determined accurately. • Replace cartridge and contact customer service. E32 Incompatible cartridge Cartridge type is incompatible with this instrument or software. • Make sure that you have the correct cartridge type for this instrument. E33 Processing memory overflow Signal processing circuits memory has overflowed. • Please execute the Clean Optics protocol (see Overview of protocols in manual mode). • Retry the measurement. E38 Cartridge not ready error The new cartridge has not been initialized correctly • Execute the “Cartridge Change” procedure (see Change cartridges). E39 Laser current limit reached The laser has reached its upper current limit; indicating end of life. • The laser needs to be replaced. Contact a service technician. E40 Set of gates not found Reference to the set of gates selected for the measurement cannot be found in the instrument settings. • The set of gates has been deleted. • Change the set of gates and retry the measurement. E41 Set of gates incompatible The set of gates selected for the measurement cannot be used with this cartridge. • Correct cartridge change procedure was not followed. • Incorrect digital input configuration. • Change the set of gates and retry the measurement. E43 External temperature too low Ambient temperature is outside of the instrument specifications. • Increase ambient temperature. • Trying to operate or store the instrument below 5 °C (41 °F) can cause damage to the device. E47 Unable to find main reference magnet during homing During initialization, the valve did not home properly. • Please contact customer service. Critical errors must be cleared manually. Make sure to first solve the origin of the problem, then manually clear the error with the steps below. Please note that the procedure below does not automatically solve the root cause of the error. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 2. Press Logs, then Error log. 3. Make sure you have resolved the problem leading to the displayed error(s). Then press the Clear errors button. 4. Cleared errors appear with grey error symbols and an “Errors cleared” event is added to the log. The instrument is ready to analyze again.

The automatic self-check tool checks that each component of the BactoSense is functioning correctly and identifies those that are not. It can be used to identify problems with the instrument. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. 3. Press the Self-check button. 4. Additional information Press the Rerun button. Once execution has terminated, the instrument shows a list of all tests, with a green PASS or red FAIL indicator. Some tests may be skipped: if the system cannot communicate with the cartridge, all the tests that require cartridge communication are skipped.

The instrument must be operated within a specific temperature range to prevent damage and ensure reliable and reproducible measurement results (see Technical data). At very low and very high ambient temperatures (below 5 °C (41 °F) or above 30 °C (86 °F)), protocols are not executed. At low ambient temperatures, the instrument automatically warms up prior to a measurement to reach the required temperature. During this heating process, the instrument status shows “Heating...”. If the target temperature cannot be reached after several hours, the protocol exits with an error (table 16-2, E42). Allow time for heating Measurements can be delayed if extensive heating is necessary. To avoid this, keep the instrument temperature above 10 °C (50 °F).

The web interface allows users to browse and export results and other data from a remote computer, as well as monitor the state of the instrument (active process, cartridge level, alerts etc.) The BactoSense needs to be connected to the same network as the computer that accesses the web interface. The web interface can be loaded on any browser on desktop computers or mobile devices. Take care about data and network security with all usual measures.

An admin must first enable HTTP or HTTPS web access under Settings → System settings → System services, apply the changes and reboot when prompted. See Retrieve files via HTTP or HTTPS for the service settings and ports. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Connect the BactoSense via Ethernet to a safe network (e.g. LAN). Connect your device (e.g. computer or tablet) to the same network. 2. On the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface, press Settings, then System info. 3. Retrieve the IP address of the BactoSense shown on the System info page. 4. On your device, open a web browser. 5. Enter http://<IP address> or https://<IP address> in the address bar, using the enabled service. Append :<port> if its port differs from the default, then press Enter. 6. On the login page, use the same username and password as for the BactoSense and press Login.

The results from multiple measurements can be downloaded as a zip file. This zip includes the FCS file and summary plots of each measurement. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the web interface, select the Results page on the navigation panel on the left. 2. Find the Online mode results or Manual mode results table for the measurements you want. 3. Select the date range for that table and click Download ZIP. A progress bar will appear at the top of the browser until the zip starts downloading. 4. Wait for the download to complete.

documents.t: The list of all results can be downloaded from the web interface in Excel XLSX, CSV or PDF format. Online mode, Manual mode and instrument validation results have separate downloads. Find the DOWNLOAD RESULTS section below the results chart and choose the row for the required measurement mode or instrument validation. 3. Click Download XLSX, Download CSV or Download PDF in that row to start the download. 4. Wait for the download to complete.

documents.t: The web interface can animate dot plots from Online mode, to help visualize the progression of the measurements. This feature shows static images in rapid succession; the animation can be exported with the Download GIF button. WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the web interface, select the Plots page on the navigation panel on the left. 2. Use the previous and next arrows or the slider to select a measurement by its timestamp. 3. Press the triangle Play button to start the animation. Press it again to pause. 4. Set Animation speed to the desired positive number of plots per second. 5. Press Download GIF to export up to 60 of the most recent Online mode plots at the selected speed. The export uses the latest plots, regardless of the slider position.
